items.title: [Bug] NPU HiCache: MHATokenToKVPoolHost crashes when the device k_buffer is a single tensor (since #40326)
items.author: pingqiu
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

`test/registered/npu/basic_function/HiCache/test_npu_hicache_mha.py` fails on `main` (PR Test (NPU), e.g. runs 37358858354 and 37376161789). The server dies while building the HiCache host pool:

```
File ".../mem_cache/pool_host/mha.py", line 160, in <genexpr>
    for buf in getattr(pool, side, None) or ()
RuntimeError: Boolean value of Tensor with more than one value is ambiguous
```

### Cause

#40326 ("Derive KV row addresses from strides, not shapes (1/7)") added this to `MHATokenToKVPoolHost.__init__`:

```python
self._init_device_row_stride(
    buf
    for pool in (self.device_pool, *self.mtp_draft_device_pools)
    if pool is not None
    for side in ("k_buffer", "v_buffer")
    for buf in getattr(pool, side, None) or ()
)
```

`... or ()` assumes `k_buffer` / `v_buffer` is a list of per-layer tensors (or `None`). The Ascend KV pool with HiCache enabled and FIA off sets them to a single multi-layer tensor (`hardware_backend/npu/memory_pool_npu.py`, `self.k_buffer = self._hicache_k_buffer`), and evaluating that tensor's truth value raises. With FIA on it uses per-layer lists, which is why only some NPU configurations hit it.

### Possible fix

Normalise the attribute before iterating, for example:

```python
def _device_buffers(pool, side):
    bufs = getattr(pool, side, None)
    if bufs is None:
        return ()
    if isinstance(bufs, torch.Tensor):
        return bufs.unbind(0)  # one entry per layer, as with the list form
    return bufs
```

and `for buf in _device_buffers(pool, side)` in the generator. Whether a per-layer view or the whole tensor is the right input to `_init_device_row_stride` on NPU is for the #40326 authors to confirm.

### Reproduction

Run `test_npu_hicache_mha.py` on an Ascend A3 runner (`--attention-backend ascend --enable-hierarchical-cache`, FIA off), as in the PR Test (NPU) workflow.

### Environment

SGLang `main` after #40326 (2026-10-01); PR Test (NPU) `base-b-test-*-npu-a3`.

Found while reading the CI results of #42399, which merged `main` but doesn't touch the host pools.

### Describe the bug

With `--enable-deterministic-inference`, the first request that sets `repetition_penalty != 1.0` kills the scheduler on `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny`. The scheduler raises inside the compiled `apply_scaling_penalties`:

items.title: [Bug] Qwen3CoderDetector streaming emits unterminated JSON arguments when the model omits `</function>`
items.author: the-Shallow
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug


The streaming parser only closes a tool call's arguments object (`}`) when it sees
`</function>`; `</tool_call>` is treated purely as a region marker. It also does not accept
`</tool_call>` as a parameter terminator. So when a model closes `</tool_call>` but omits
`</function>`, the streamed argument fragments never form valid JSON — they end mid-object
(`{"days": 0`), and if `</parameter>` is missing too the parameter is dropped entirely. The
non-streaming path recovers the arguments correctly in both cases.


### Reproduction


```python
import json

from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
from sglang.srt.function_call.qwen3_coder_detector import Qwen3CoderDetector

tools = [
    Tool(
        type="function",
        function=Function(
            name="get_current_weather",
            parameters={"type": "object", "properties": {"days": {"type": "integer"}}},
        ),
    )
]

texts = {
    "no </function>": "<tool_call>\n<function=get_current_weather>\n"
    "<parameter=days>\n0\n</parameter>\n</tool_call>",
    "no </function> and no </parameter>": "<tool_call>\n<function=get_current_weather>\n"
    "<parameter=days>\n0\n</tool_call>",
}

for label, text in texts.items():
    oneshot = Qwen3CoderDetector().detect_and_parse(text, tools)
    det = Qwen3CoderDetector()
    streamed = "".join(
        c.parameters
        for ch in text
        for c in det.parse_streaming_increment(ch, tools).calls
        if c.parameters
    )
    print(label)
    print("  oneshot:", oneshot.calls[0].parameters)
    print("  stream :", repr(streamed))

# no </function>
#   oneshot: {"days": 0}
#   stream : '{"days": 0'                <- not valid JSON, missing '}'
# no </function> and no </parameter>
#   oneshot: {"days": 0}
#   stream : ''                          <- argument dropped entirely
```

### Expected behavior and impact

* Both parsing paths in this module are written to tolerate a model that drops closing tags.
  `detect_and_parse` has an explicit fallback alternative for it
  (`r"<function=(.*?)</function>|<function=(.*)$"`), and the streaming parameter scanner
  documents the same intent:

  ```
  # A parameter can end in multiple ways:
  # 1. [Normal] Encounter </parameter>
  # 2. [Abnormal] Encounter next <parameter=
  # 3. [Abnormal] Encounter </function>
  ```

  `</tool_call>` belongs to that same class of abnormal terminators but is missing from the
  candidate list, and there is no corresponding "close the object" handling in section 5.
* The consequence is not a degraded value but a protocol violation: `serving_chat.py` forwards
  `call_item.parameters` verbatim as the `arguments` delta, so the client accumulates
  `{"days": 0` and fails to `json.loads` the finished tool call. `Qwen3CoderDetector` never
  populates `prev_tool_call_arr` / `streamed_args_for_tool`, so
  `_check_for_unstreamed_tool_args` cannot backfill the missing `}` either.
* The same model output parses fine in non-streaming mode, so the request succeeds or fails
  depending only on `stream=True/False`.

### Suggested fix

Treat `</tool_call>` as a parameter terminator, and close an open arguments object when the
tool-call region ends.

```diff
--- a/python/sglang/srt/function_call/qwen3_coder_detector.py
+++ b/python/sglang/srt/function_call/qwen3_coder_detector.py
@@ -314,10 +314,12 @@ class Qwen3CoderDetector(BaseFormatDetector):
                     # 1. [Normal] Encounter </parameter>
                     # 2. [Abnormal] Encounter next <parameter=
                     # 3. [Abnormal] Encounter </function>
+                    # 4. [Abnormal] Encounter </tool_call>
                     # So we need to find the smallest one as the parameter end position.
                     cand_end_param = rest_of_slice.find(self.parameter_end_token)
                     cand_next_param = rest_of_slice.find(self.parameter_prefix)
                     cand_end_func = rest_of_slice.find(self.function_end_token)

items.title: [Bug] Qwen3CoderDetector streaming parser fabricates tool calls from plain text, emitting `tool_index=-1
items.author: the-Shallow
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug


`parse_streaming_increment` matches `<function=` and `<parameter=` anywhere in the stream,
without requiring an enclosing `<tool_call>` block. Ordinary assistant prose that mentions the
tool-call syntax is therefore parsed as a tool call: the text is stripped from `normal_text`
and emitted as tool-call deltas. When the text contains a `<parameter=` without a preceding
`<function=`, `current_tool_id` is still `-1`, so the deltas go out with `index=-1` and no
`id`/`name`. The non-streaming path (`detect_and_parse`) and `has_tool_call` both correctly
treat the same text as plain text.


### Reproduction


```python
from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
from sglang.srt.function_call.qwen3_coder_detector import Qwen3CoderDetector

tools = [
    Tool(
        type="function",
        function=Function(
            name="get_current_weather",
            parameters={"type": "object", "properties": {"location": {"type": "string"}}},
        ),
    )
]

text = "The format is <parameter=location>Boston</parameter> okay?"

det = Qwen3CoderDetector()
print(det.has_tool_call(text))
print(det.detect_and_parse(text, tools))
print(Qwen3CoderDetector().parse_streaming_increment(text, tools))

# False
# normal_text='The format is <parameter=location>Boston</parameter> okay?' calls=[]
# normal_text='The format is  okay?' calls=[ToolCallItem(tool_index=-1, name=None, parameters='{'),
#                                           ToolCallItem(tool_index=-1, name=None, parameters='"location": "Boston"')]
```

### Expected behavior and impact

* `has_tool_call` is defined as `"<tool_call>" in text`, and `detect_and_parse` returns early
  with `normal_text=text` when that token is absent. The module therefore defines "no
  `<tool_call>` token" as "no tool calls"; the streaming path contradicts its own non-streaming
  path for byte-identical model output, so a request differs purely on `stream=True/False`.
* The `is_inside_tool_call` flag was added for exactly this purpose (`"[FIX] New state flag:
  mark whether inside tool_call structure block"`), but it only gates the *normal-text*
  branches (sections 1 and 6); the tag-matching branches (sections 2–4) ignore it.
* `tool_index=-1` is not a valid OpenAI streaming index.
  `serving_chat.py` passes it straight through as `ToolCall(index=call_item.tool_index, ...)`
  with `id=None` and `name=None`, so the client receives an argument delta for a tool call it
  was never told about, under a negative index. SDKs that accumulate deltas by index either
  drop it or raise.
* Text is also lost: the prose that got consumed as tags is removed from `normal_text` and
  never delivered to the user.

### Suggested fix

Gate the structural-tag branches on `is_inside_tool_call`, and only hold back a partial
`<tool_call>` prefix when outside a tool call. With this applied, the offending text is emitted
verbatim as `normal_text` and no calls are produced.

```diff
--- a/python/sglang/srt/function_call/qwen3_coder_detector.py
+++ b/python/sglang/srt/function_call/qwen3_coder_detector.py
@@ -275,7 +275,9 @@ class Qwen3CoderDetector(BaseFormatDetector):
             # -------------------------------------------------------
             # 2. Function Name: <function=name>
             # -------------------------------------------------------
-            if current_slice.startswith(self.tool_call_prefix):
+            if self.is_inside_tool_call and current_slice.startswith(
+                self.tool_call_prefix
+            ):
                 end_angle = current_slice.find(">")
                 if end_angle != -1:
                     func_name = current_slice[len(self.tool_call_prefix) : end_angle]
@@ -303,7 +305,9 @@ class Qwen3CoderDetector(BaseFormatDetector):
             # -------------------------------------------------------
             # 3. Parameter: <parameter=name>value...
             # -------------------------------------------------------
-            if current_slice.startswith(self.parameter_prefix):
+            if self.is_inside_tool_call and current_slice.startswith(
+                self.parameter_prefix
+            ):
                 name_end = current_slice.find(">")
                 if name_end != -1:
                     value_start_idx = name_end + 1
@@ -387,7 +391,9 @@ class Qwen3CoderDetector(BaseFormatDetector):
             # -------------------------------------------------------
             # 4. Function End: </function>
             # -------------------------------------------------------
-            if current_slice.startswith(self.function_end_token):
+            if self.is_inside_tool_call and current_slice.startswith(
+                self.function_end_token
+            ):
                 if not self.json_started:
                     calls.append(
                         ToolCallItem(tool_index=self.current_tool_id, parameters="{")
@@ -429,14 +435,17 @@ class Qwen3CoderDetector(BaseFormatDetector):
             elif next_open_angle == 0:
                 # Looks like a Tag, but doesn't match any known Tag above
 
-                possible_tags = [
-                    self.tool_call_start_token,
-                    self.tool_call_end_token,
-                    self.tool_call_prefix,
-                    self.function_end_token,
-                    self.parameter_prefix,
-                    self.parameter_end_token,
-                ]
+                possible_tags = (
+                    [self.tool_call_start_token]
+

items.title: [HiCache] NVFP4 KV + kernel io-backend: host pool row geometry mismatch and block scales never transported (packed MTP draft silently corrupted, accept length pinned to 1.0)
items.author: chengye75-star
items.body_excerpt:
**Environment**: Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 checkpoint (GDN hybrid, 16 full-attention layers + packed NEXTN draft layer → 17), TP2, `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-write-policy write_through --hicache-io-backend kernel --hicache-mem-layout page_first --page-size 64 --speculative-algorithm NEXTN`. Reproduced deterministically on v0.5.21; **the same geometry is still present on current `main`** (`pool_host/mha.py:219-222` sizes host rows from device *element* counts; no FP4-aware host pool exists under `pool_host/`).

### Symptom

Once a large resident prefix is evicted to the L2 host pool and loaded back, speculative decoding dies **silently and permanently**:

- `spec_accept_length` pins to ~1.00 (healthy 2.0–3.0); greedy probes accept 0 extra tokens
- target outputs stay byte-exact correct — only the restored draft KV is garbage
- decode throughput drops ~25% *below* the no-MTP baseline (draft tax, zero benefit)
- no crash, no warning; `/flush_cache` does not recover; only a process restart heals

Hit a production box after 3 h of normal traffic (trigger event: one ~137K-token request pushing pool usage to 0.86). Then reproduced at **cycle 0, 3/3 runs** with the battery below.

### Root cause (convicted by on-engine probes + offline byte-exact synthesis)

NVFP4 device pools store **packed** fp4: one device row holds `row_dim / 2` **bytes** (2 elements/byte, `store_dtype=uint8`), e.g. `k_buffer[l] : (size, 2, 128)` = 256 B/token, while per-block scales live in *separate* tensors (`k_scale_buffer[l] : (size, 2, 16)`).

`MHATokenToKVPoolHost.get_size_per_token()` sizes the host row as `head_num * head_dim * itemsize` with `head_dim` in **elements** → 512 B/token, and the HiCache JIT kernels are launched with one shared `element_size` (`self.element_dim * itemsize` / `token_stride_size`) for both sides. The kernels cannot express the asymmetry:

1. **H2D (`load_to_device_per_layer`)** views the 256 B device row as half of a 512 B element: token *i* lands at device rows `2*i`, an in-range guard truncates the copy (measured in-engine at production scale: 14.5 MB of live bytes, only ~64 KB written — the rest of the load is a NO-OP),
2. **D2H (staged write-back)** gathers 512 B spans off 256 B-stride rows, pairing two device tokens per host row,
3. **`k_scale_buffer` / `v_scale_buffer` are never moved at all** by the `kernel` path — even a correctly addressed payload dequantises with stale scales after loadback.

Because the MTP draft layer is packed at the tail of the same pool (#30393 path), *every* restored draft row is garbage while target layers mostly re-fill from re-prefill — hence "target correct, draft dead, accept = 1.0 forever".

`--hicache-io-backend direct` is **immune** (it goes through `get_page_buffer_meta`, which segments data/scale per page), which is the current community workaround.

Key in-engine evidence (probe logs in attached bundle):

```
V17 LOAD slot=80000 n=56704  host_before=c77cc863…  poison=dab32424…  dev_after=dab32424…  -> LOAD-NOOP
V18 load_to_device_per_layer layer_id=16 io=kernel layout=page_first jit=True is_draft=True
    row_before=00492333cd row_after=00492333cd  -> NO-OP (function runs, kernel writes nothing)
V21 D2H on stock: 64 backed-up tokens rewrite 128 device rows (double-pitch), scale tensors untouched
Offline synthesis (engine geometry, real host-pool class + real JIT kernels):
    host 512B vs device 256B, element_dim=512 -> token i -> device rows 2i/2i+1   (repro)
    control host 256B <-> device 256B                                             -> byte-exact
```

Ruled out with controls each: transfer kernel itself (offline byte-exact on square geometry), stream races (forced H2D-after-D2H still corrupts), host-slot preemption (zero range overlaps detected), stale packed pointer tables / index translation (snapshot == live at the corrupting H2D).

### Deterministic reproduction

Two sessions over a ~197K-token corpus (`dual.py` in attached bundle):

1. warm: 137K-token prefix, `max_new=1` (usage → 0.85)
2. press: remaining ~60K with `max_new=8000`; decode evicts session-A pages to host (write_through)
3. recall: re-send A's prefix → host→device loadback
4. probe: greedy counting request; accept mean over its decode window

Stock + `kernel` backend: `accept_mean` collapses to 1.0–1.16 at cycle 0, 3/3. `layer_first` layout avoids the double-pitch (square contract there) — the defect is specific to `page_first` + packed-fp4 rows + missing scale transport.

### Fix + verification

A dedicated host pool `MHATokenToKVPoolFP4Host` (prototype: `chengye75-star/sglang` branch `fix/hicache-nvfp4-main`, one commit, +426 lines, mirrors the existing `MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8Host` precedent):

- host payload rows sized in **device bytes** (`head_dim // 2`, `dtype=uint8`) → every JIT element size is square on both sides; payload transfers stay inherited from the base class, packed-MTP handling included;
- block scales ride **page-granular side buffers** moved by the same staged page kernels (both the interleaved `[token, head, dim]` and TRT-LLM-native `[page, head, token, dim]` layouts are page-local);
- draft layer packs into the tail layer of payload *and* scale buffers;
- non-page-multiple transfers zero the touched host scale pages (never restore stale scales);
- L3 flat-storage interfaces raise `NotImplementedError` (same boundary MXFP8 keeps).

Results on the incident config:

| battery | stock `kernel` | fixed `kernel` |
|---|---|---|
| offline byte-exact round-trip (payload+scales, position-encoded, 9792 B/token) | n/a | **PASS** |
| 4× dual-session evict/loadback, probe accept | 1.11 → 1.00 (cycle 0) | **3.00 / 3.00 / 2.99 / 3.00** |
| 10× multi-turn 137K pressure, accept mean | corrupted on long runs | **2.32–2.86, engine healthy** |
| throughput | 29 t/s collapsed | 78–89 t/s |

Note the detection trap for reviewers: the device pool is the plain `MHATokenToKVPoo

items.title: [Bug] Glm47MoeDetector streaming emits invalid JSON for array/object/boolean values that aren't strict JSON ("1, 2", "True", empty)
items.author: Shreyasg13
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

In `Glm47MoeDetector` (`--tool-call-parser glm47`, GLM-4.7 / GLM-5), the streaming path passes `array`, `object` and `boolean` argument values through verbatim, assuming the model wrote valid JSON. The non-streaming path runs the same values through `parse_arguments`, which salvages non-JSON spellings. So when the model writes a value that isn't strict JSON, non-streaming returns valid arguments, but streaming emits **invalid JSON** in `delta.tool_calls[].function.arguments`:

| param type | model wrote | non-streaming | streaming |
|---|---|---|---|
| array | `1, 2` | `{"a": [1, 2]}` | `{"a": 1, 2}` ❌ |
| array | `"x", "y"` | `{"a": ["x", "y"]}` | `{"a": "x", "y"}` ❌ |
| boolean | `True` / `False` | `{"b": true}` | `{"b": True}` ❌ |
| array / object | (empty) | `{"a": ""}` | `{"a": }` ❌ |

Clients that `json.loads` the accumulated arguments (most agent frameworks) fail on the call, while the same request without `stream=True` succeeds.

### Reproduction

CPU-only, no model needed (current main, 20bf93b):

```python
from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import Function, Tool
from sglang.srt.function_call.glm47_moe_detector import Glm47MoeDetector

props = {"a": {"type": "array"}, "b": {"type": "boolean"}}
tools = [Tool(type="function", function=Function(
    name="f", parameters={"type": "object", "properties": props}))]

for key, value in [("a", "1, 2"), ("b", "True")]:
    text = f"<tool_call>f<arg_key>{key}</arg_key><arg_value>{value}</arg_value></tool_call>"
    non_stream = Glm47MoeDetector().detect_and_parse(text, tools).calls[0].parameters
    d = Glm47MoeDetector()
    stream = "".join(c.parameters for ch in text
                     for c in d.parse_streaming_increment(ch, tools).calls)
    print(f"non-stream={non_stream}  stream={stream}")
```

Output:

```
non-stream={"a": [1, 2]}  stream={"a": 1, 2}
non-stream={"b": true}  stream={"b": True}
```

Across a small grid (array/object/boolean/string/number values × chunk sizes 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and whole), 36 of 132 streamed outputs are invalid JSON on main.

`Glm4MoeDetector` (`glm45`) has the same pattern in its own streaming code, and also streams `number` values verbatim (`1,000` for a number param streams as `{"n": 1,000}`). This issue is about `glm47`; GLM-4.5 would need a separate change.

### Environment

sglang main @ 20bf93b; Python 3.13; CPU-only (parser code, no GPU needed).

items.title: [Feature] Metrics to localize bottlenecks in the multi-tokenizer / multi-detokenizer IPC path
items.author: hope1262946533
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [ ] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation


## Background

With `--tokenizer-worker-num > 1` and `--detokenizer-worker-num > 1`, requests and streamed outputs pass through several processes connected by ZMQ:

```text
Input:  TokenizerWorker (M processes) → MultiTokenizerRouter → Scheduler
Output: Scheduler → MultiDetokenizerRouter (1 process) → detokenizer worker (N processes) → TokenizerWorker (M processes) → HTTP response
```

When one stage of the output path saturates, completed outputs wait in the ZMQ queues between processes. In a closed-loop workload, which is typical for benchmarking and for many production clients, a request releases its client concurrency slot only after its final output arrives. A slow output path therefore reduces the number of requests reaching the scheduler. The symptoms appear in **scheduler** metrics, while the cause sits in the output path.

Current metrics cannot show which stage is saturated. This feature request asks for basic per-stage metrics on this IPC path.

## Current gaps

1. **`MultiDetokenizerRouter` exports no metrics.** It runs as a separate process (`sglang::detokenizer_router`) with a single synchronous event loop. It does not start the CPU monitor thread and has no counters, histograms, or gauges. Its CPU usage, message rate, per-message processing time and input queue backlog are not observable.
1. **Detokenizer workers are only visible as an aggregate.** The only detokenizer metric is `sglang:process_cpu_seconds_total{component="detokenizer"}`, sampled every 5 seconds. All N workers report under the same label set, so one overloaded worker cannot be distinguished from evenly spread load. There is no processing-time or queue-latency metric for this stage.
1. **Per-worker load skew is not visible.** The router pins requests to detokenizer workers with `crc32(http_worker_ipc) % N`, so load on detokenizer workers and TokenizerWorkers can be uneven. TokenizerWorkers likewise all report CPU under `component="tokenizer"`. No metric reports requests or CPU per worker.
1. **Latency metrics do not separate the stages.** TokenizerManager-side metrics such as `sglang:inter_token_latency_seconds` and `sglang:e2e_request_latency_seconds` include every upstream delay. They cannot tell whether time was spent in the scheduler, the router queue, the detokenizer, or the TokenizerWorker.

As a result, a saturated output path is easily misread as "the client is not sending enough load" or "the scheduler cannot fill the batch". Raising `--detokenizer-worker-num` does not help when the router is the bottleneck, because it only adds workers downstream of the single router process, and the current metrics give no hint of this.

For completeness: `MultiTokenizerRouter`, which forwards every request from TokenizerWorkers to the scheduler and relays scheduler-to-tokenizer messages back to the owning TokenizerWorker, also has no dedicated metrics. We have no measurement suggesting that it has been a bottleneck. It is mentioned only so that both routers can be covered consistently if router metrics are added.

## Observed case

Deployment: SGLang 0.5.17 (`29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`), DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP8/DP8, no MTP, decode-only with fake transfer, decode CUDA Graph maximum batch size 310, `max_running_requests=2480` (310 per rank), tokenizer/detokenizer workers 32/32, `stream_interval=1`.

Client: closed-loop streaming generate requests, concurrency 4960, 79,360 requests, input/output lengths 60,000/1,000. All requests succeeded and the server log contained no errors.

1. **What the existing metrics showed:** running requests per rank stayed well below 310, with mean 186.73 and p50/p90/p95/p99 of 187/253/284/310. The prealloc, transfer and waiting queues were all empty in 96.29% of the samples. Client median TTFT was 94.18 s. Taken together, these signals suggest insufficient incoming load or a scheduler-side admission problem.
1. **What was actually happening:** the bottleneck was only found with temporary out-of-tree tracing that timestamped every final output at seven points along the output path:
    1. The scheduler's local send returned in 0.61 ms (p50), but the wait between scheduler send and router receive was 89.88 s at p50 and 100.00 s at p99.
    1. During the stable phase, 3,100-3,200 completed requests were queued at the router input. These requests still held client concurrency slots, which left only 93-215 requests per rank for the scheduler.
    1. Router CPU p50 was 127.5%, and 87.4% of the router loop time was spent processing messages. The router was saturated.
1. **Raising the worker count did not help.** In a separate run with the same workload, raising detokenizer workers from 32 to 64 left the Batchsize dips in place, and the prealloc queue p50 stayed at 0. This is consistent with a router bottleneck, but none of the existing metrics could have pointed there.
1. **Load skew was also not visible.** Requests from 28 active HTTP workers mapped onto only 19 of the 32 detokenizer workers. One TokenizerWorker received 14,853 requests and ran at 103.8% CPU (p50). One detokenizer worker ran at 91.4% CPU (p50). The aggregated CPU metrics show none of this.

The router send path itself is addressed separately by #42238. This request is only about observability: the next saturation on this path, wherever it occurs, should be visible from metrics without custom tracing.

## Proposed metrics

Ordered from cheapest to most informative:

1. **Router CPU:** start the existing CPU monitor in `MultiDetokenizerRouter`, for example `sglang:process_cpu_seconds_total{component="detokenizer_router"}`. A value pinned near or above one core directly indicates router saturation.
1. **Per-worker identity:** add a worker label (for example

items.title: [Bug]: Hidden-state extraction inflates KV cache memory requirements by 24× on a hybrid Mamba/MLA model
items.author: stormchasingg
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Enabling `extract_hidden_states` with Model Runner V2 on a Kimi-K3 hybrid Mamba/MLA model fails during KV cache initialization.

The hidden-state cache contains one logical layer, but each of its blocks is charged at the width of the largest target-model cache group: 24 layers. This increases its memory contribution from approximately **5.40 GiB to 129.61 GiB**, exceeding available memory.

This is a KV cache admission failure, rather than a CUDA allocation exception.

### Environment

- Model: Kimi-K3, hybrid Mamba/MLA
- Runner: Model Runner V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`)
- Local vLLM base: `41172e5e47`, with V2 extraction support ported from #49811
- Tensor parallelism: 16
- Extraction dtype: BF16
- Hidden-state connector: custom Mooncake connector
- `max_model_len`: 65536
- `mamba_cache_mode`: `none`

The failure was reproduced on this local branch. It has not been reproduced against an unmodified current upstream checkout.

### Error

```text
ValueError: To serve at least one request with the model's max seq len
(65536), (131.36 GiB KV cache is needed, which is larger than the
available KV cache memory (29.24 GiB).
```

### Diagnostic breakdown

All groups have a physical page size of **442368 bytes**.

| Group | Spec | Layers | Tokens/block | Blocks needed | Admission contribution |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | MambaSpec | 23 | 65536 | 2 | 0.0198 GiB |
| 1 | MambaSpec | 23 | 65536 | 2 | 0.0198 GiB |
| 2 | MambaSpec | 23 | 65536 | 2 | 0.0198 GiB |
| 3 | MLAAttentionSpec | 24 | 384 | 171 | 1.6908 GiB |
| 4 | HiddenStateCacheSpec | 1 | 5 | 13108 | **129.6079 GiB** |

The extraction cache stores six hidden-state vectors per token, each of size 7168:

```text
bytes_per_token = 6 × 7168 × 2 = 86016
tokens_per_page = floor(442368 / 86016) = 5
page_padding = 12288 bytes

hidden-state pages alone:
13108 × 442368 = 5.4003 GiB
```

However, the shared pool uses the maximum group width:

```text
group_size = 24
required_bytes = group_size × page_size × sum(blocks_needed_per_group)
```

Consequently, the singleton extraction group pays for 23 unused layer slots on every block:

```text
hidden-state contribution = 24 × 5.4003 GiB = 129.6079 GiB
total requirement = 131.3580 GiB
```

### Suspected cause

In the affected grouping path:

1. `HiddenStateCacheSpec` is excluded from target-model grouping.
2. The 69 Mamba layers are divided into three groups of 23.
3. The 24 MLA layers form one group.
4. The hidden-state cache is appended as a singleton group, with its page size aligned to the target groups.
5. Both physical allocation and admission accounting use the largest group width.

The shared pool layout therefore introduces substantial unused capacity for the extraction group. Changing only the admission formula would not fix the physical allocation layout.

### Local workaround and observed result

We modified the extraction grouping path to split target groups into singleton groups before appending the hidden-state group:

```python
# vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py
def get_kv_cache_groups(
    vllm_config: VllmConfig, kv_cache_spec: dict[str, KVCacheSpec]
) -> list[KVCacheGroupSpec]:
    ...
    if hidden_specs:
        groups = [
            replace(group, layer_names=[name])
            for group in groups
            for name in group.layer_names
        ]
    ...
```

This preserves per-layer cache specs and uses the existing shared block pool with one-layer-wide blocks.

Observed diagnostics after the change:

```text
extraction uses single-layer cache groups:
target_groups=4->93 hidden_groups=1

max_model_len=65536
groups=94
max_group_layers=1
available_GiB=29.2441
required_GiB=7.1480
```

The engine successfully starts with extraction enabled.

This validates removal of the admission failure. Extracted hidden-state numerical equivalence and throughput impact have not yet been validated. Singleton grouping increases block-table and scheduler overhead, so it may not be the best general solution.

### Additional comparison

A run without extraction starts with a 2.3298 GiB requirement. However, it has 29 MLA layers and eight blocks per Mamba layer, compared with 24 MLA layers and two blocks in the extraction run. It is therefore not a controlled extraction-only A/B comparison.

### Expected behavior

Adding a singleton hidden-state cache should require storage proportional to its own data, without multiplying that storage by the number of layers in the widest target cache group.

Could the grouping or allocation scheme accommodate this case without requiring one cache group per target layer—for example, through separate pools or a layout that avoids unused layer slots?

### Related

- #49811 — Model Runner V2 support for hidden-state extraction.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bug]: GLM-5.2-FP8 + prefix caching + FP8 KV cache returns empty content (gibberish reasoning) on repeated identical prompts
items.author: liangjason87
items.body_excerpt:
### Your current environment
The output of python collect_env.py, reconstructed from startup ```text ============================== vLLM Version ============================== vLLM Version : 0.27.1 (V1 engine; system_fingerprint "vllm-0.27.1-tp8-...") ============================== Model / Serving ============================== Model : zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 (GlmMoeDsa, sparse-MLA / sparse_attn_indexer) served_model_name : zai-org--glm-5.2-fp8 dtype : torch.bfloat16 quantization : fp8 kv_cache_dtype : fp8_e4m3 tensor_parallel_size : 8 pipeline_parallel_size : 1 max_model_len : 524288 max_num_seqs : 32 gpu_memory_utilization : 0.8 enforce_eager : False cudagraph_mode : FULL_AND_PIECEWISE enable_prefix_caching : True enable_chunked_prefill : True speculative_config : None # no MTP / speculative decoding reasoning_parser : glm45 tool_call_parser : glm47 enable_auto_tool_choice : True moe_backend : aiter linear_backend : aiter custom_ops : ['+quant_fp8','+grouped_topk','+sparse_attn_indexer', ...] ============================== Hardware / Platform ============================== GPU : AMD Instinct MI300X x8 (ROCm / AITER backends) Engine image : hf-vllm-v0-27-1-amd (AMD build) ============================== Notable startup log lines ============================== [cache.py:296] Using fp8_e4m3 data type to store kv cache. ... it may cause accuracy drop without a proper scaling factor [mla_attention.py:522] Sparse MLA impl has no dense-MHA prefill path; using the top-k MQA path only. ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug ## 🐛 Bug Sending the **same** ~43k-token request repeatedly: first N (fresh prefill) are correct, then once it hits the prefix cache a response comes back with `content: null`, an **incoherent multilingual `reasoning`** field, and `finish_reason: "stop"` — silent, no traceback. Prepending a unique prefix (forces fresh prefill) → **0/50 failures**. So the trigger is **prefix-cache reuse**, not length, parsing, weights, or MTP. ### Repro ```bash vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --max-model-len 524288 --max-num-seqs 32 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 --enable-prefix-caching \ --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 ``` ```python import json import urllib.request import uuid BASE = "http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions" MODEL = "zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8" SYS = ( "You are an interactive agent. Prefer dedicated file tools over shell. " "Before writing a file you MUST load the design skill. External scripts " "load only from approved CDNs. Never impersonate a real person or " "organization. " ) * 350 def body(system): return { "model": MODEL, "messages": [ {"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": "hi"}, ], "max_tokens": 4000, "temperature": 0, "stream": False, } def call(payload): req = urllib.request.Request( BASE, data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, ) return json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=180).read()) def classify(message): content = (message.get("content") or "").strip() return "EMPTY" if content == "" else "ok" print("identical (cache hits):") for i in range(1, 300): out = call(body(SYS)) msg = out["choices"][0]["message"] label = classify(msg) print(i, label, out["usage"]["completion_tokens"]) if label != "ok": print(json.dumps(msg, ensure_ascii=False)[:600]) break print("unique prefix (fresh prefill):") for i in range(1, 51): out = call(body(uuid.uuid4().hex + SYS)) print(i, classify(out["choices"][0]["message"])) ``` ### Observed **Identical prompt (prefix-cache hits)** — fails on the 13th request: ```text identical (cache hits): [012] ok completion_tokens=85 [013] EMPTY completion_tokens=129 ``` The failing response: `content` is null and `reasoning` is gibberish, yet `finish_reason` is `"stop"`: ```json { "role": "assistant", "content": null, "reasoning": ", samoch3,1columnfk7help\">9 ... 、seb0 might8ひ7-" } ``` **Unique prefix (fresh prefill)** — all clean: ```text unique prefix (fresh prefill): [001] ok ... [050] ok # 50/50 clean ``` ## Expected A prefix-cache hit must not corrupt generation; repeated identical requests should return consistent, coherent output. ## Suspected area Prefix-cache reuse + `fp8_e4m3` KV cache + sparse-MLA top-k MQA prefill under CUDA graphs. Can A/B `--enforce-eager`, bf16 KV, or prefix caching off if useful. ## Potentially Related #59926 (v0.27.1, fp8 KV, prefix-cache reuse; cache_salt helps — closest), #50881 (FP8 KV garbage under CUDA graphs), #60174 (prefix-cache hit corrupts output). ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Misc]: CMake Clean-up / Refactor Tasks
items.author: LucasWilkinson
items.body_excerpt:
In an effort to make the CMake more readable, stable and easy to use we have a few tasks we'd like to work on, creating a GitHub issue here to track that progress, some planned changes/investigations:

- [ ] Rename `define_gpu_extension_target`, currently this is used for CPU extensions too so the name is now misleading
- [ ] Add a CI test of local builds, i.e. `pip install -e .`
- [ ]  Warn that PTX builds are not currently supported (post https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/8845), currently if there is a `+PTX` in `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` this will be ignored. We should warn when this is the case. Alternatively we can add support for PTX builds although this is generally not desirable since PTX increases the wheel size by quite a bit (PTX is larger than SASS), and we already build for all currently supported arches.
- [ ]  Have vllm-flash-attn use [ExternalProject](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/module/ExternalProject.html) currently vllm-flash-attn uses the parent CMake scope which creates many footguns since it is in a separate repo, using `ExternalProject` will mean that the vllm-flash-attn will be run in a separate CMake scope/process
  - [ ] It might be even better to revert to the FlashMLA approach, where CMake code lives in vllm.
- [ ] Look into removing early returns in CMakeLists.txt (potentially move backends into its own files)
- [ ] Potential build both C++ and CUDA extensions when building for CUDA and using torch dispatcher to dispatch between the two, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/8424

items.title: [Bug] --enable-linear-replayssm forces no_buffer, which degrades mamba prefix caching and inflates TTFT up to 4.7x
items.author: davidli1515
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist - [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. - [x] The bug persists in the latest version. - [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback. - [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed. - [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed. ### Describe the bug ## Describe the bug `--enable-linear-replayssm` requires `--mamba-radix-cache-strategy no_buffer`. That strategy stores the mamba checkpoint at a radix-tree depth later requests cannot reach, so prefix reuse collapses and TTFT rises sharply on any workload with a shared prefix. ### Measured Qwen3.8-27B, 1×H200, TP=1, `sglang.benchmark.serving`, `--request-rate 8 --max-concurrency 48`. Both arms use `--disable-overlap-schedule`, because `no_buffer` asserts against the overlap scheduler; holding it fixed keeps the cache strategy the only variable. - **default** = `extra_buffer`, no ReplaySSM (what most users run today) - **replayssm** = `--enable-linear-replayssm`, which forces `no_buffer` | workload | arm | prefix cache hit | out tok/s | TTFT mean | TTFT p99 | E2E mean | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | **rag**
2048-tok shared prefix
(8 groups × 32) | default | **88.2%** | 509.6 | 226.4 ms | 1788.2 ms | 2164.7 ms | | | replayssm | **65.9%** | 508.7 | **1062.6 ms** | **4116.2 ms** | 3876.4 ms | | | | | −0.2% | **+369%** | **+130%** | **+79%** | | **fewshot**
512-tok shared prefix
(32 groups × 8) | default | **62.2%** | 510.1 | 83.0 ms | 261.5 ms | 1959.6 ms | | | replayssm | **0.0%** | 508.9 | **159.0 ms** | **622.3 ms** | 3048.2 ms | | | | | −0.2% | **+92%** | **+138%** | **+56%** | | **sharegpt**
real conversations,
little cross-request sharing | default | 0.7% | 1136.7 | 95.9 ms | 476.6 ms | 7145.5 ms | | | replayssm | 0.0% | 1162.6 | 97.0 ms | 477.8 ms | 6929.3 ms | | | | | +2.3% | +1.1% | +0.3% | −3.0% | Hit rate is `cached / (cached + new)` summed over the server's own `Prefill batch ... #cached-token:` lines. ShareGPT is the control: consecutive requests share almost nothing, both arms sit near a 0% hit rate, and the two configurations become indistinguishable. The gap only appears where prefixes are actually shared, which is what confirms the regression comes from prefix reuse and not from some other effect of the flag. ### Why output throughput is flat Throughput is unchanged in every row, but that is a property of the load point, not evidence that the regression is free. At `--request-rate 8` with 64-token outputs the offered rate is ~512 tok/s for the two `generated-shared-prefix` runs, and measured throughput is 508–510: the server delivered exactly what arrived, so throughput was pinned by the arrival rate rather than by the server. The ShareGPT rows in the same table reach 1137–1163 tok/s on the same server, which alone shows capacity is more than twice what the shared-prefix runs asked for. Below saturation the extra prefill work has nowhere to go except queueing delay, so it lands entirely on **TTFT and E2E**. At saturation it would convert into a throughput loss instead. ### Mechanism `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/components/mamba_component.py:529-533` chooses the tree depth the mamba checkpoint is attached to: ```python if self.cache.enable_mamba_extra_buffer: cache_len = req.mamba_last_track_seqlen # a boundary reached DURING the prompt else: # no_buffer cache_len = token_ids_len # prompt + this request's OWN generated tokens ``` Requests share a *prompt*; their generated continuations differ. Under `no_buffer` the checkpoint sits past the end of the prompt, so a follow-up request walks the tree only to the end of its own prompt, lands on a node that carries no mamba value, and the mamba match validator rejects it. Because a forward pass resumes from a single position for all layers, a missing mamba anchor also discards the KV hit. Instrumenting the match path on a 601-token prompt whose predecessor stored 608: ``` insert: finished=True token_ids_len=608 -> cache_len=608 match: full_kv_hit_length=600 mamba_boundary=0 branching_seqlen=576 result: #new-token: 601, #cached-token: 0 ``` KV alone could have reused 600 tokens. It reused none. Severity scales with shared-prefix length: with a 512-token prefix the hit rate goes to exactly 0%, while with a 2048-token prefix it only falls to 65.9% — long prefixes contain enough grid-aligned positions that some reuse survives. ### Is this intended? `no_buffer` avoids the extra ping-pong buffer, so trading memory for reduced cross-request reuse could be deliberate. If it is, could the trade-off be documented and could the `--enable-linear-replayssm` guard mention it? Users enabling ReplaySSM for decode bandwidth are unlikely to expect a TTFT regression of this size. If it is not intended, the guard's own comment points at the cause — `donate_mamba_ping_pong_slot` (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:1454`) never resets `replayssm_write_pos`, unlike `MambaPool.copy_from` (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py:997`), which is why `python/sglang/srt/server_args.py:6357` refuses `extra_buffer`: > the extra_buffer ping-pong donation path is not yet supported (follow-up) I have a candidate fix along those lines (two edits, ~7 lines) that restores the hit rate and TTFT to the default arm's numbers with GSM8K accuracy parity over 1319 questions and a clean 6.5-hour soak. I will open it as a PR referencing this issue. ### Scope of verification - Reproduced on **UnifiedRadixCache** (`Init Unified Radix Cache. Components: (FULL, MAMBA). Tree Core: UnifiedTreeCore`). The legacy `MambaRadixCache` has the same code shape (`mamba_component.py` notes it "Mirrors `MambaRadixCache.cache_finished_req`") but I have not tested

items.title: [Bug]: Wrong timestamps if audio > 30s
items.author: dr75
items.body_excerpt:
### Your current environment


NA

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Segment level timestamps are incrementally offset by ~0.5s per segment.**

When transcribing long audio with vLLM Whisper, segment-level timestamps are increasingly inaccurate. Chunking uses by default a 1s window to find low-energy (quiet) regions for splitting, so the next chunk may start up to 1s earlier than the nominal chunk length. This offset is not compensated for when generating segment timestamps, resulting in an average delay of ~0.5s per segment, which accumulates (e.g., 5s after 10 segments).

Clients can workaround by subtracting 0.5s per segment, but that's obviously not accurate.

Also, the [related documentation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e83b7e379c11bf136c1b96bc6a67b6d2207cfde4/docs/contributing/model/transcription.md#audio-preprocessing-and-chunking) is not correct: there are no overlapping chunks, but just a window for searching the best split point. Maybe this confusion is the cause of the issue.

TORCHINDUCTOR_COMPILE_THREADS=1
TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/torchinductor_root
```
</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The `--kv-cache-memory` value that vLLM prints at startup double-counts CUDA-graph memory whenever `VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS=1` (the default). For models with a large CUDA-graph pool the suggested value comes out **negative**, so it cannot be used and, since #47374, it also silently defeats `VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1`.

#### Background: what the `--kv-cache-memory` recommendation is

`--kv-cache-memory` (config `kv_cache_memory_bytes`) lets the operator hard-code the KV cache size in bytes. When set, vLLM skips the memory-profiling measurement and the CUDA-graph memory estimation pass, and reserves exactly that amount instead of deriving it from `--gpu-memory-utilization` (a short `profile_run()` for compilation still happens). The value is only meaningful if it reproduces the current allocation: too optimistic and the engine OOMs at graph capture, too conservative and batch concurrency (hence throughput) is capped. It is valid only on the same GPU with the same initial free memory.

Because the profiled value is deterministic for a fixed (model, config, hardware, library) combination, `gpu_worker.py` recomputes the exact `--kv-cache-memory` that reproduces the current allocation on every boot and logs it at INFO (promoted from DEBUG in #47374, "Surface the --kv-cache-memory suggestion at INFO and document fast-startup knobs"). The message offers two numbers:

```
Replace gpu_memory_utilization config with `--kv-cache-memory=<X>` (<X> GiB) to fit into
requested memory, or `--kv-cache-memory=<Y>` (<Y> GiB) to fully utilize gpu memory.
```

`X` fills up to the `--gpu-memory-utilization` target; `Y` uses all free device memory. Both are meant to be copied back verbatim, and `X` is also what the opt-in `VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1` feature (same PR, #47374) persists under `$VLLM_CACHE_ROOT/startup_plan/` to skip profiling on subsequent boots. That feature's guard rejects non-positive recorded values, so a negative `X` makes the whole fast-startup mechanism inert for exactly the models that would benefit most.

#### Impact

- The copy-paste `--kv-cache-memory` suggestion is unusable (negative) on large-graph models.
- `VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1` records the negative value and its guard rejects it, so fast startup is a silent no-op.
- No OOM: the double count only affects the reported recommendation, not the live allocation (`Current kv cache memory in use` is still correct).

### Reproduction

Serve any model whose CUDA-graph pool is large relative to the device — e.g. a DeepSeek-class MoE with dspark/MTP speculative decoding (`num_speculative_tokens=5`, 85 + 81 capture sizes) — and read the startup memory-profiler line. Here `--gpu-memory-utilization` was left at its 0.92 default, TP=8:

```
Free memory on device (175.81/178.35 GiB) on startup. Desired GPU memory utilization is
(0.92, 164.08 GiB). Actual usage is 58.44 GiB for consumed memory (weights + non-torch),
62.33 GiB for peak activation, and 63.99 GiB for CUDAGraph memory. Replace
gpu_memory_utilization config with `--kv-cache-memory=-22362854379` (-20.83 GiB) to fit
into requested memory, or `--kv-cache-memory=-9766683136` (-9.1 GiB) to fully utilize gpu
memory. Current kv cache memory in use is 43.31 GiB.
```

The engine runs fine with 43.31 GiB of KV cache, yet both suggested values are negative. The same run also logs:

```
CUDA graph pool memory: 63.99 GiB (actual), 57.45 GiB (estimated), difference: 6.55 GiB (10.2%).
```

### Root cause

The allocation path counts CUDA-graph memory once; the suggestion path counts it twice.

Allocation path — `determine_available_memory` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py`):

```python
self.peak_activation_memory = (
    profile_result.transient_peak_headroom + cudagraph_memory_estimate_applied
)
...
self.available_kv_cache_memory_bytes = (
    self.requested_memory
    - profile_result.non_kv_cache_memory          # = total_consumed + transient_peak_headroom
    - cudagraph_memory_estimate_applied
)
```

Suggestion path — `compile_or_warm_up_model` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py`):

```python
non_kv_cache_memory = (
    self.total_consumed
    + self.peak_activation_memory          # already contains cudagraph_memory_est

items.title: [Bug] Layerwise blender reuses stale singleton state and staging buffers across requests — crashes under variable-length load
items.author: matu79go
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

The layerwise blender (`lmcache/v1/compute/blend/blender.py`) keeps per-request state on a singleton and reuses GPU staging buffers without length checks. Sequential same-length requests work, but a sustained stream of **variable-length** requests reliably kills the EngineCore. We hit three distinct failure modes; minimal defensive patches for each are included below (they let a 900-request variable-length replay run to completion).

## Environment

- LMCache main @ `668a1fd` (source build), vLLM 0.19.1, Llama-3.1-8B, `--enforce-eager`, blending enabled via `LMCacheConnectorV1` (with the model-registration workaround from the companion issue)
- Workload: RAG-style replay, requests = 1–7 documents (~84–1500 tokens each) joined by the blend separator, arrival-driven load

## Failure modes

### 1. `get_kv` returns a pooled staging buffer containing the previous request's rows

`process_qkv` does:

```python
old_k, old_v = self.gpu_connector.get_kv(layer_id)
diff_k = torch.sum((k - old_k) ** 2, dim=[1])
```

`get_kv` returns the **whole** buffer (`buffer_mapping[layer_id].tensor`). When the previous request retrieved more tokens than the current one, stale rows remain and shapes mismatch:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (512) must match the size of tensor b (262) at non-singleton dimension 0
```

Fix that worked: slice `old_k/old_v` to the blend's original token length. Note the slice length must be recorded at layer 0 — after the check layer, `q` shrinks to the top-k rows, so slicing by `q.shape[0]` corrupts the `old_k[imp_indices] = k` scatter (we learned this the hard way: device-side assert).

### 2. `LMCBlendMetadata` is only cleaned on successful completion

`blend_layer` calls `self.metadata.clean()` at the end of a *successful* pass. After any mid-blend exception, `positions` / `imp_indices` survive into the next request:

```
# next request, rotary embedding:
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (768) must match the size of tensor b (651) ...
```

Fix: call `self.metadata.clean()` at `blend()` entry.

### 3. Not reentrant under batch-queue pipelining

With vLLM's async scheduling (`step_with_batch_queue`), two in-flight steps can interleave blends on the same singleton blender/metadata, producing the same class of mismatch even with fixes 1–2 in place. `--no-async-scheduling` avoids it; a per-request metadata object (or a lock around `blend()`) would be the real fix.

Also worth noting: an exception anywhere in this path propagates out of `start_load_kv` and takes the whole engine down (`EngineDeadError` → every subsequent request 500s). Treating a failed blend as a per-request load failure would make the blast radius much smaller.

Happy to share our exact patches or turn them into a PR.

items.title: [Bug] Native connector worker death leaves L2 adapter pending maps and L1 read locks stuck
items.author: Writtic
items.body_excerpt:
**Label**

Please label as `bug`.

**Summary**

`ConnectorBase`'s worker loop can exit with requests still queued, and nothing tells the Python side. Every `future_id` submitted to that worker then sits in `NativeConnectorL2Adapter`'s pending maps for the life of the process, and for stores it also pins the L1 read locks the in-flight task holds.

Raised in review on #4211 by @maobaolong. Filing it separately as agreed there, since the fix belongs to the C++ completion contract rather than the adapter.

**Details**

The adapter pairs every insert into `_pending_ops`, `_pending_store_sizes`, and `_pending_store_tasks` with a removal: the submit failure path cleans up its own entries, and the demux thread pops all three when a completion arrives. The maps grow without bound only when a submitted `future_id` never produces a completion.

`worker_loop_for_queue` in `csrc/storage_backends/connector_base.h` has two such paths:

1. `create_connection()` throws before the request loop starts. The outer `catch` prints to stderr and the worker returns, leaving its queue undrained.
2. A non-`std::exception` escapes the per-tile `catch (const std::exception&)`, unwinds to `catch (...)`, and kills the worker. That tile never reaches `handle_tile_completion`.

Both report through `fprintf(stderr, ...)` instead of the logger, so a dead worker is easy to miss.

For stores the cost is larger than dict growth. `StoreController` records `read_locked_keys` per in-flight task and releases them on completion, so a task that never completes holds L1 read locks until the process exits and those chunks cannot be evicted.

**Expected Outcome / Goal**

Every submitted `future_id` gets exactly one completion, including when its worker dies. Options worth discussing:

- On worker exit, drain the queue and push a failed `Completion` for each pending request.
- Widen the per-tile catch to `catch (...)`, so an unknown exception fails one tile instead of the worker.
- Report worker death through the logger and a metric, not only stderr.

**Actual Outcome**

The maps grow without bound and the store task never completes. #4211 adds `lmcache_mp.l2_adapter_pending_entries`, a gauge over the three maps per adapter, which makes this visible: a series that keeps climbing without returning to zero is this leak.

items.title: [Bug] fs L2 adapter: every store fails at os.open() in _write_with_odirect when use_odirect=true
items.author: h1manshu23
items.body_excerpt:
**Describe the bug**
With the `fs` L2 adapter and `use_odirect: true`, **every** chunk store fails. `FSL2Adapter._write_with_odirect` raises at the `os.open()` call, and each store is logged as failed:

```
[2026-07-31 12:39:27,361] LMCache ERROR: FSL2Adapter failed to store
/mnt/nvme0/-SEP-data-medium-SEP-text-generation-models-SEP-gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-dynamic-SEP-@0x01000100@1@246ba704d24a7690450504e0a607656c195b4e247501896d103d7d293f9b63dc.data
(fs_l2_adapter.py:629:lmcache.v1.distributed.l2_adapters.fs_l2_adapter)
```

Nothing is ever persisted to L2, so the disk tier is effectively dead while the server continues running and reporting no fatal error.

**This is not an unsupported-storage case.** `base_path=/mnt/nvme0` is a real block-backed filesystem on a 4-device NVMe RAID0 array:

```
md0 : active raid0 nvme3n2[3] nvme2n2[2] nvme1n2[1] nvme4n2[0]
```

Two distinct problems here:

1. **The failure itself.** O_DIRECT should be usable on this mount. Whatever LMCache passes to `os.open()` — flag combination, mode, or path — is being rejected on a filesystem/device stack that otherwise accepts direct I/O.
2. **The failure is undiagnosable and unrecoverable.** The log line prints the target path but not the underlying `OSError`/errno, so there's no way to tell EINVAL from EACCES from ENOENT without reading LMCache's source. And there is no fallback: rather than degrading to buffered I/O or refusing at startup, the adapter fails silently-but-endlessly, once per chunk, for the lifetime of the server.

Note the failure is at **`os.open()`**, not at the write — so this is not an O_DIRECT buffer/offset/length alignment issue, which would surface later in `_write_with_odirect`.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. `base_path` sits on a 4× NVMe md RAID0 (512k chunk) mounted at `/mnt/nvme0`.

2. Start the LMCache server with the `fs` L2 adapter and O_DIRECT enabled:

```bash
lmcache server --host localhost --port 9000 \
  --l1-size-gb 128 --eviction-policy LRU --chunk-size 256 \
  --l2-adapter '{"type": "fs", "base_path": "/mnt/nvme0", "use_odirect": true, "num_workers": 32}' \
  --http-port 8081
```

3. Start vLLM against it on a single GPU:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve /path/to/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-dynamic/ \
  --port 9001 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill \
  --max-model-len 16384 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"LMCacheMPConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"lmcache.mp.host":"tcp://localhost","lmcache.mp.port":9000}}' \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 12
```

4. Send any request. Every L2 store fails with the traceback below; `/mnt/nvme0` stays empty.

**Expected behavior**

On a direct-I/O-capable filesystem like this one, stores should succeed with `use_odirect: true` — that's the whole point of running the cache on NVMe RAID0.

Failing that, LMCache should:
- include the underlying errno / `OSError` message in the `failed to store` log line, and
- probe `O_DIRECT` support on `base_path` **once at startup**, then either fail fast with an actionable message or fall back to buffered I/O — instead of raising per-chunk for the lifetime of the process.

**Screenshots**

items.title: [Documentation Request] vLLM kv_load_failure_policy doesn't apply to load failures in L2 adapters
items.author: RedL0tus
items.body_excerpt:
**Label**
Please label your issue so that it can easily be easily categorized under [LMCache Onboarding](https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/issues/1882)

**Summary**
[kv_load_failure_policy](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/api/vllm/config/kv_transfer/#vllm.config.kv_transfer.KVTransferConfig.kv_load_failure_policy) doesn't seem to apply to remote KV data load failures in L2 adapters.

**Details**
vLLM supports setting kv_load_failure_policy, which defines the behavior during KV load failures. However, this configuration option doesn't seem to apply to L2 adapters. We've tested the `nixl_store` L2 adapter and the `s3` L2 adapter with injected errors, and LMCache seems to treat L2 load failures as cache misses instead of failures.

is this an intentional design choice? It would be great to document the expected behavior of failures at different cache levels in LMCache.

**Steps / Reproduction (if applicable)**
1. Start LMCache with L2 adapter set to `nixl_store` with OBJ backend, or `s3`.
2. Start vLLM, use LMCache for KV cache offloading and internal prefix caching disabled with `--no-enable-prefix-caching`.
3. Send data to vLLM and Intercept all GetObject calls to the S3 endpoint.

**Expected Outcome / Goal**
With `"kv_load_failure_policy": "fail"`, requests with external cache hits should return error code.

**Actual Outcome (if applicable)**
LMCache log errors to the console, vLLM proceed to serve all requests with recomputed KV data as if it's only a cache miss.

**Additional Context**
This issue was first discovered by [Anish Sana](mailto:anish.sana@hpe.com) under HPE's internal testing.

items.title: L1 eviction races async L2 store: chunks discarded before offload are never stored (persistent re-prefill under L1 pressure)
items.author: ShreyasBaasri07
items.body_excerpt:
**Label**
Bug

**Describe the bug**
In LMCache v0.5.5 (MP mode), under L1 (CPU) memory pressure, freshly-computed KV chunks can be evicted from L1 before the asynchronous store controller offloads them to L2, so they are silently dropped and never written to L2 — even when L2 is large enough to hold the entire working set and has no eviction configured.

The result: with a shared-prefix (prefix-caching-style) workload, ~19% of requests permanently retrieve only the shared prefix (first half of the prompt) and re-prefill the unique tail on every recurrence, indefinitely. The half-hits persist through the whole run, not just warmup.

Root cause (confirmed in v0.5.5 source):

L1 eviction destination defaults to EvictionDestination.DISCARD — L1 eviction does not offload to L2 (lru.py, eviction_controller.py:193).
The StoreController offloads L1→L2 by reserve_read-ing keys received from an L1_WRITE_FINISHED notification. If a key was already discard-evicted in the meantime, reserve_read returns KEY_NOT_EXIST, the key is silently skipped from the store (only surfaced as an L1_READ_FAILED / lmcache_mp.l1_read_failure "not_found" anomaly), and it never reaches L2 (lmcache/v1/distributed/storage_controllers/store_controller.py:600-627).
So there is a race between L1 DISCARD eviction and the async L2 offload; the loser is silently never stored.

**To Reproduce**
Environment: LMCache v0.5.5, MP mode, L1 + L2 where L2 is sized to hold the full working set and has no L2 eviction, and L1 is smaller than the shared-prefix working set.

Start the LMCache MP server with a small L1 and one large L2 adapter (e.g. S3/filesystem), no L2 eviction:
lmcache server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 6555 --chunk-size 256 \
  --l1-size-gb 60 --eviction-policy LRU \
  --l2-adapter '{"type":"s3", ... ,"max_capacity_gb":500}'

Start vLLM with LMCacheMPConnector (kv_role: kv_both), --no-enable-prefix-caching --enforce-eager.
Run a shared-prefix benchmark whose prefix pool exceeds L1. With aiperf/genai-perf
--prefix-prompt-length 4096 --num-prefix-prompts 150 \
--isl 4096 --osl 100 --num-dataset-entries 200 \
--concurrency 10 --random-seed 42 --benchmark-duration 1200

Here 150 prefixes × 4096 tokens ≈ 75 GB of prefix KV > 60 GB L1. Each request = 8192 tokens (4096 shared prefix + 4096 unique tail).

Grep the server log for Retrieved N tokens.

Observed — persistent prefix-only half-hits throughout the run (not just warmup)
Half-hits occur at ~20–32/min even in steady state, long after every one of the 200 fixed prompts has been served many times. Since retrieval is a contiguous match from token 0, Retrieved 4096 means "prefix found, tail missing → prefill." (Optionally, lmcache_mp.l1_read_failure / L1_READ_FAILED "not_found" events fire in the same window.)

Control: setting --num-prefix-prompts 10 (prefix pool now fits in L1) eliminates the half-hits — all requests become full 8192-token hits. So the trigger is specifically L1 < shared-prefix pool.

**Expected behavior**
Once a chunk is computed and admitted to L1, it should reliably be offloaded to L2 and remain retrievable regardless of L1 pressure. A chunk should not be silently dropped from the L2 store just because it was evicted from L1 before the async offload read it. Subsequent requests for the same prompt should be full L2 hits, not re-prefills, when L2 has capacity and no eviction.

**Screenshots**
N/A (server-side KV-cache behavior; log evidence included above).

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
OS: Linux
LMCache: v0.5.5
vLLM: 0.26.0
PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130
Python: 3.12.3
GPU: NVIDIA L40S
Mode: MP (LMCacheMPConnector, kv_role: kv_both), --chunk-size 256, --l1-size-gb 60, L2 sized to hold full working set with no L2 eviction

**Smartphone (please complete the following information):**
N/A (not a mobile/browser issue)

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.

items.title: Restart-proof KV cache for llama-server: 40K-token TTFT 155s to 6s after reboot
items.author: qqkzlm
items.body_excerpt:
Every restart wipes your prefill. Server crash, box reboot, model reload — a 40K-token agentic prompt pays the full ~155s prefill again before the first token.

I patched llama-server to persist KV-cache prefix checkpoints to disk and auto-restore the longest matching prefix on boot. Same prompt after a restart: **first token in ~6s instead of ~155s** (2.1s disk read once + decode). No client changes, no re-architecture — the server just remembers.

Measured on GTX 1080 8GB, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, `-c 92160`:

- Cold: 151s prefill → first token at ~155s
- Warm (post-restart): 2.1s disk read (first request only) → first token at ~6s
- Checkpoints keyed by model + ctx + KV quant (wrong config = ignored, never corrupted); disk-budget eviction included

Single-commit patch (86KB): https://github.com/qqkzlm/llama-cpp-prompt-disk-cache — `git am` onto the PrismML `prism` branch, four flags (`--slot-save-path`, `--checkpoint-min-step`, `--ctx-checkpoints`, `--prompt-cache-disk-budget`).

One MoE lesson from the same box: keep experts on GPU, let KV follow the layers — pushing 20 MoE layers to CPU collapsed prefill 265→30 tok/s, which no cache can fix.

Happy to upstream behind a flag if maintainers are interested.

comments.author: qqkzlm
comments.body:
Update to the README since this went up — three things worth calling out for anyone trying it:

**1. Prebuilt CUDA binaries exist for both platforms.** The `v0.2.3` release ships `llama-server-win-cuda-v0.2.3.zip` and `llama-server-linux-cuda-v0.2.3.tar.gz`. The Linux package is built for `sm_61`/Pascal, so it also runs on GTX 10-series. No build needed:

```bash
./llama-server -m model.gguf -c 32768 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --slot-save-path /var/tmp/kvstore/model \
  --prompt-cache-disk-budget 20 --checkpoint-min-step 2048 --ctx-checkpoints 64
```

**2. Only one flag is actually required.** `--slot-save-path` is the only one you must pass — `--prompt-cache-disk-budget` and `--prompt-cache-disk-path` are silently ignored without it, and entries land in `<slot-save-path>/pdcache`. `--prompt-cache-disk` is **enabled by default**, so passing it is optional; use `--no-prompt-cache-disk` to turn the cache off.

**3. Cache hits require a byte-identical prompt prefix.** Only the common prefix from token 0 onward is reused. If you prepend a timestamp or a random ID, everything after it misses and the cache is effectively unused. Put stable content first (system prompt, tool definitions, long docs) and per-turn content last — opencode / Claude Code already do this, so it works out of the box.

The README now has a "when does the cache hit / when does it miss" section covering this, a flag-duty table, and a Chinese-first three-step guide (the repo README is now Chinese-primary). A Windows `start-llama-server.bat` is included in the zip if you want a prompt-driven launcher instead of a command line.

Still happy to upstream this behind a flag if maintainers are interested — the whole feature is one commit touching `tools/server/server-prompt-disk.cpp` (~900 lines) plus slot/task integration.

items.title: [Bug] --strip-thinking-cache + retraction: release_kv_cache frees KV slots the radix tree still owns (double free)
items.author: sohom-cs
items.body_excerpt:
**Describe the bug**

With `--strip-thinking-cache`, `Req.owned_kv_len()` caps the owned length at the prompt once the request has reasoning tokens (#22373):

```python
if get_serving().strip_thinking_cache and self.reasoning_tokens > 0:
    return min(self.kv.kv_committed_len, len(self.origin_input_ids))
```

`release_kv_cache` then treats `[owned_kv_len, kv_allocated_len)` as over-allocated and frees it (`_release_overallocated_kv_indices`). That relies on nothing past the prompt being in the tree, i.e. on `cache_protected_len <= len(origin_input_ids)`.

A retracted request breaks that. It keeps `output_ids` and `reasoning_tokens` (`reset_for_retract` resets neither) and is re-prefilled over `prompt + output_ids`. After that prefill, `maybe_cache_unfinished_req` → `cache_unfinished_req` inserts the whole re-prefill, so `cache_protected_len = len(prompt) + len(earlier output)`. When the request finishes, or is retracted again:

- `cache_finished_req(owned_kv_len=P)` / `free_kv_row([(cache_protected_len, P)])` frees nothing, since `cache_protected_len > P`;
- `_release_overallocated_kv_indices(P, kv_allocated_len)` frees `[P, kv_allocated_len)`, and that includes `[P, cache_protected_len)`, which belongs to a tree node.

With `page_size > 1` and a prompt that doesn't end on a page boundary, the same thing happens through a different free: `cache_finished_req` frees its unaligned tail `[page_aligned(owned_kv_len), owned_kv_len)`, and that page is also tree-owned once `cache_protected_len > P` (e.g. page 4, P=10, `cache_protected_len`=12: the page holding positions 8–11 is freed while the tree keeps it).

Those slots are now both in the free list and referenced by the tree. When the node is evicted they are freed again. `available_size()` can exceed the pool size, and one `alloc()` can hand the same slot to two requests: silent KV corruption. The assert that would catch it (`start_p == end_p`) is skipped under `strip_thinking_cache`.

The PD decode resume path looks exposed in the same way (`process_prebuilt` caches the resumed request with `maybe_cache_unfinished_req`), but I have reproduced only the aggregated path.

**Reproduction** (CPU, main `0967a013c2a`, `UnifiedRadixCache`, 256-slot pool, prompt 8, 6 output tokens before the retraction, 3 decode steps after the re-prefill; real `cache_unfinished_req`, `release_kv_cache`, `evict`)

```
after re-prefill: cache_protected_len=14 (prompt=8)
owned_kv_len()=8 committed=17 allocated=17
[finish] available after release: +9 (expected +3)
[finish] slots freed while still referenced by the tree: [9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14]
[finish] after evicting the tree: free list 262 entries, 256 unique; available_size 262 > pool 256
[finish] one alloc() of the whole pool hands out [9..14] twice
```

The same numbers with `is_insert=False` (a second retraction).

**Expected:** each KV slot is freed once.

**Proposed fix:** under `strip_thinking_cache`, never report less than `cache_protected_len`:

```python
return min(self.kv.kv_committed_len, max(len(self.origin_input_ids), self.kv.cache_protected_len))
```

The output the tree already holds (from the re-prefill) stays the tree's, and only the request-private tail is freed. Without a retraction, `cache_protected_len <= prompt`, so behaviour is unchanged.

I have this with a CPU test (finish, second retraction, the no-retraction case, and page_size=4 with aligned and unaligned prompts). I'm filing the issue first because two open PRs touch this code: #41281 (@hnyls2002) and #35694 (@alphabetc1), which changes `owned_kv_len`. The test still fails on the current heads of both (`1c912a5d6bb` and `5724c337c00`), and passes on both with the one-line change. In #41281's `insert_req` flow, `cache_protected_len` is lowered to the page-aligned `P` before the tail free, so the tree-owned slots are still freed. Happy to send it as a PR on top of whichever lands first, or for it to be folded into one of them.

items.title: [RFC][NPU] INT8 (C8) KV cache for DSA models (GLM-5.2) on Ascend A2/A3 (910B/910C)
items.author: qidaye
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

This RFC proposes generalizing the existing arch35-only packed FP8 DSA KV cache
to a "packed one-byte quant" path, so that GLM-5.2 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`) and
other DeepSeek-V3.2-style DSA models can run an **INT8 (C8) KV cache on Ascend
A2/A3 (910B/910C)**. Every hardware question the proposal depends on has been
probed on a 910B (CANN 9.0.0, torch_npu 2.10.0); section 4 states measured
verdicts, not predictions.

Sections 1-4 of the full RFC follow. The remaining sections (change-surface
audit, test plan, confidence ledger) exist and can be posted here if useful;
a few forward references to them ("section 5" / "section 6" / "section 7")
remain in the text below -- the "section 7" material is summarized under
**Proposed contribution plan** at the end.

> All `file:line` references are against `sgl-project/sglang` at
> **`06008c170dae333e22caceb51f36224071f9b5b3`** (`[dsv4.1]Optimize FP4 indexer by
> skipping invisible tiles`, #40431), which is an ancestor of `upstream/main` --
> so every citation below is checkable against upstream as-is.
>
> vllm-ascend references are against **`abe8ff18a96bcd5f90d08077d1ccd068b959cab4`**
> and carry a `[va]` prefix, relative to that repo's root.
> ops-transformer references are against `gitcode.com/cann/ops-transformer` at
> **`bcc6304656c9e712b50b1faa22872a158b1e34c5`** (the commit sgl-kernel-npu's CI
> pins; `bcc6304` below) and carry an `[ops-t]` prefix.

## 1. Motivation

SGLang today supports an 8-bit ("C8") KV cache for DSA models on Ascend **only on
arch35 / Ascend 950**, in the FP8-E4M3 packed form added by
`[NPU]Support GLM5.2 and FP8 DSA&Indexer kvcache for 950` (commit `3ff226ba8f`).
On A2/A3 the DSA KV cache is unconditionally BF16.

This matters because the KV cache is the binding constraint on A2-class hardware.
A representative single-node deployment (8x 910B, 64 GB/card, GLM-5.2-W4A8, TP8,
`--mem-fraction-static 0.85`):

| item | per card |
|---|---|
| weights | 49.67 GB |
| KV cache | 1.73 GB -> `max_total_num_tokens = 16768` |
| NPU graphs | 0.75 GB |
| unused | 8.25 GB |

`context_len` is 1 M, but the whole instance holds ~16 K tokens. Raising
`mem-fraction-static` helps, but the ceiling is still set by BF16 KV bytes/token.

Per token, per layer, for GLM-5.2 (`kv_lora_rank=512`, `qk_rope_head_dim=64`,
`index_head_dim=128`):

| component | BF16 | INT8 packed | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| main MLA latent + rope | 1152 B | 656 B (512 int8 + 4x fp32 tile scales + 64x bf16 rope) | **1.76x** |
| indexer K | 256 B | 130 B (128 int8 + 1x fp16 scale) | **1.97x** |
| **total** | **1408 B** | **786 B** | **1.79x** |

The main-KV term dominates, so the expected end-to-end gain is ~1.6-1.8x more
resident tokens at the same memory budget. vllm-ascend reports a **measured
1.62x** for the equivalent change on GLM-5 W8A8 / A3 (75,600 -> 122,309 tokens,
PR #11228 / #11846) -- a second-hand figure from PR prose, but consistent with
the arithmetic above.

---

## 2. What exists today

### 2.1 The arch35 FP8 packed path (the template)

Storage is an **opaque fixed-width record**, one per token per layer, whose width is

```python
# python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_configurator.py, calculate_mla_kv_cache_dim
kv_lora_rank + kv_lora_rank // quant_block_size * 4 + qk_rope_head_dim * rope_storage_dtype.itemsize
# GLM-5.2: 512 + 4*4 + 64*2 = 656 bytes
```

It is produced by `_pack_dsa_fp8_kv_cache`
(`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/memory_pool_npu.py:839`):

```python
quantized, scale = torch_npu.npu_dynamic_quant(latent.reshape(-1, 128), dst_type=self.dtype)
packed = torch.cat((quantized.view(uint8),            # 512 B
                    cache_v.to(bf16).view(uint8),     # 128 B  rope, NOT quantized
                    scale.to(fp32).view(uint8)),      #  16 B  4 per-128-tile scales
                   dim=-1)
```

and consumed by `forward_sparse`
(`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_backend.py:1228`):

```python
torch_npu.npu_kv_quant_sparse_flash_attention(
    query=torch.cat((q_nope, q_pe), -1),   # bf16 [T, H, 576]
    key=packed, value=packed,
    key_quant_mode=2, value_quant_mode=2,
    key_dequant_scale=None, value_dequant_scale=None,   # scales read inline
    quant_scale_repo_mode=1, tile_size=128, rope_head_dim=64,
    layout_query="TND", layout_kv="PA_BSND", sparse_mode=3, attention_mode=2, ...)
```

**Key observation: the record layout is not FP8-specific.** It is "512 one-byte
values + per-128-tile FP32 scales + BF16 rope tail", and INT8 and FP8-E4M3 are
both one byte, so the 656-byte width, the `quant_scale_repo_mode=1` /
`tile_size=128` descriptor, and the `npu_dynamic_quant` call site
(`dst_type=self.dtype` already) carry over structurally. The quantization is
**dynamic** (per-token, per-128-tile, computed online), so no checkpoint
calibration is required.

The scale contract is settled, from two independent implementations: the
**main-KV** per-128-tile scale is **FP32 for INT8 and FP8 alike**, symmetric,
no zero-point (`[va] vllm_ascend/attention/utils.py:87-99` hardcodes an fp32
scale term in the record width regardless of KV dtype;
`[va] vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py:1991` has the INT8 branch cast the scale
`.to(torch.float32)`). The **indexer** per-token scale is a different buffer
entirely -- FP16 under INT8 on A2/A3, FP32 under FP8 on A5 -- and belongs to
section 2.2, not to this record.

Functional acceptance of this record with an INT8 payload on a 910B is now
