items.title: Agentic Cache Scheduling System Roadmap (Q4)
items.author: hzh0425
items.body_excerpt:
## 1. Agentic Cache Scheduling

- Supernode-wide KV Cache Sharing @hzh0425  @Shunkangz
	- Enable sharing of GPU-resident (L1) and host-resident (L2) KV caches across engines within the same NVLink domain.
	- Add cache location awareness to the Router to coordinate request placement and KV transfers based on cache availability and engine load.
	- Extend HiCache linker integration to support GPU-to-GPU KV transfers over NVLink and remote Grace DRAM access through EGM.
	- Optimize small KV-page transfers and NUMA placement; validate correctness, cache hit rate, and TTFT/TPOT on GB200 and GB300/ AMD Rack.
- Build a KV cache orchestrator across the router and engine @ZhaiFeiyue 
	- Identify sessions, sub-agents, and tool calls, and expose `PREFETCH`, `DEMOTE`, and `PIN` hints for global cache scheduling. Align this work with the [[router roadmap](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25760)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25760). 
	- Add session-aware scheduling to the router
- Enhance HiCache Linker Mode @hzh0425 @alphabetc1 @huangtingwei9988 
    - Support fast failover and recovery.
    - Extend support to hybrid models with Mamba and SWA.
    - Improve reliability and observability for production deployment.
    - Refactor `hybrid_pool_assembler.py`：Simplify pool assembly and improve extensibility across model architectures.
- Support a [[unified KV cache layout](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33651)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33651) for host cache and L3 storage: @Shunkangz @huangtingwei9988 
    - [[PR #39727](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39727)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39727): Add a page-unified host KV layout and topology-independent L3 keys.
    - [[PR #39726](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39726)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39726): Add a JIT kernel to load page-unified host KV back to the device one layer at a time.
    - [[PR #39815](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39815)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39815): Integrate page-unified host pools and storage keys with the HiCache linker.

## 2. Decode Prefix Cache @jojoakm @HZY-Wade 

- Refactor the decode-side HiCache mixin to support L1-only, L1+L2, and L2-only cache configurations.
- Support an L2-only `DecodeRadixTree` to increase KV transfer batch sizes and reduce GPU memory pressure ([[PR #38292](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38292)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38292)).
- Extend the decode-side unified radix tree to fully support SWA, Mamba, and MTP.

## 3. Unified KV Cache Sharding for CP @Shunkangz @HZY-Wade 

- [[PR #38356](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38356)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38356): Add logical-page placement and a rotated allocator to distribute KV pages across shard ranks.
- [[PR #37615](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37615)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37615): Add sharded KV pools that store each rank’s owned pages and assemble the full prefix for prefill attention.
- [[PR #38468](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38468)](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38468): Wire KV cache sharding into prefill scheduling and capacity checks.
- PR #42973: Extend CP KV cache sharding to GLM DSA and MTP, with P/D transfer and CPU HiCache support for both KV and indexer caches. @HZY-Wade 
- PR #43057: Fuse DSA indexer quantization with scratch/local writes and reuse raw FP8 latent staging, preserving fallbacks for unsupported layouts.  @HZY-Wade 
- Support unified kvcache layout for dcp.

## 4. HiSparse @alphabetc1   @bingps  @Shunkangz 

- Develop HiSparse V2 to coordinate GPU and host memory as a larger decode cache, targeting up to **2× KV capacity** in GB deployments.
- Refactor HiSparse to support more sparse attention model variants through a common architecture.
- Optimize the HiSparse swap-in kernel by overlapping KV prefetch with computation to reduce the performance impact of cache I/O.
- Integrate with TBO, h2d overlap moe
- hisparse compatibility(mtp/dspark/hicache/decode radix/pp)

## 5. **Unified Engram Storage**  @hzh0425 @stmatengss 

- Unify table storage and lookup for DeepSeek Engram, Qwen PLE, and LongCat N-gram embeddings under `mem_cache`, preserving model-specific hashing and computation.
- Support GPU, host-memory, and file-backed storage through common interfaces for table loading, sharding, quantized lookup, and memory accounting.
- Unify batched lookup and asynchronous prefetch to overlap table access with model execution.
- Integrate with existing request-state lifecycle management and extend toward cross-instance table sharing within a supernode.

## 6. SGLang KVCache Simulator @littlefatfat 

- [ ] Support multi-instance simulation for distributed cache scheduling and P/D disaggregation.
    - [x] Support BLOCKING mode.
    - [ ] Synchronize global logical clocks across nodes in OFFLINE mode.
- [ ] Model network latency and bandwidth contention across KV transfers, cache prefetching, and shared-cache access.

items.title: SM120: FlashInfer autotune exceeds NCCL pair timeout — all workers crash after ~50 min with "Application timeout caused pair closure"
items.author: xzwgit
items.body_excerpt:
## Environment

- GPU: 8× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120, cc 12.0)
- Driver / CUDA: 595.71.05 / CUDA 13.2.2
- FlashInfer: 0.7.1 (source build from main, with CUTLASS/CCCL headers linked per #5873)
- vLLM: nightly dev511, `--kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"flashinfer_cutlass"}'`

## Problem

The first-boot FlashInfer autotune (`mxfp8_gemm`, 21 profiles) runs for >50 minutes on SM120. During this time, the 8 TP workers' NCCL pairs are idle and exceed the timeout threshold. When the autotune finishes and the warmup dummy run starts calling `flashinfer_cutlass_fused_moe`, the NCCL communication is already dead:

```
RuntimeError: Application timeout caused pair closure
```

All 8 workers crash simultaneously. The AutoTuner itself completes successfully (21/21 profiles at ~230 profile/s) — the crash happens in the subsequent warmup phase.

## Timeline

| Phase | Duration | Status |
|---|---|---|
| FlashInfer JIT compilation | ~15 min | ✅ |
| AutoTuner (mxfp8_gemm, 21 profiles) | ~27 min | ✅ completes |
| Warmup dummy run | — | ❌ NCCL already dead |

## Workaround

`--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` (same flag used in the RTX PRO 6000 recipes for other models). Service starts in ~1 minute, correctness verified (17×19=323), FlashInfer CUTLASS kernels work without tuning.

However, this means SM120 users get untuned kernels. On B300 (SM100), autotuned FlashInfer is 30~54% faster than DeepGEMM; without autotune on SM120, FlashInfer is only +8~12% faster at c8+ and -5~11% slower at c1~c4.

## Suggested fix

One of:
1. Increase NCCL timeout during autotune (or set NCCL_KEEP_ALIVE or similar)
2. Make autotune communicate periodically with NCCL pairs to keep them alive
3. Run autotune in a separate process before starting the engine (pre-tune CLI tool)
4. Warn users about this timeout and auto-set `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune` on SM120 when first boot is detected

This issue is distinct from #5873 (missing headers) — both must be fixed for a smooth SM120 first-boot experience.

items.title: Feature Request: Add an sm_86 entry to the MMVQ cutoff table (Q4_0 crosses at 7 on A10, worth 9.1%)
items.author: zhihz
items.body_excerpt:
### Prerequisites - [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well. - [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md). - [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed). - [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share. ### Feature Description

I ran into this while checking whether the conclusions in #26079 hold on Ampere. That PR added per-architecture MMVQ cutoffs tuned on 4090, 5090 and GB10, and as far as I could tell it decided that Q4_0 and Q8_0 don't need a lowered cutoff because mvq stays ahead through the whole batch range. On my A10 that isn't quite true at the top of the range.

Short version: at ne11 == 8, forcing the quantized matmuls to MMQ instead of MMVQ gets me 9.1% more prompt throughput on a pure Q4_0 Llama-3.1-8B. Below 8 the current behaviour is clearly right, and MMVQ wins by as much as 1.57x, so this is only about the last step.

The selection lives in ggml_cuda_should_use_mmvq() in ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmvq.cu. It matches on exact compute capability, and there are branches for Ada Lovelace, Blackwell, DGX Spark, CDNA1 and CDNA2. sm_86 doesn't match any of them, so it falls off the end into

    return ne11 <= MMVQ_MAX_BATCH_SIZE;

which is 8 (mmvq.cuh:3). So on an A10 every quantized matmul with 8 columns or fewer goes to MMVQ, and that last step is the one that looks wrong.

Numbers

Three binaries out of the same tree at commit 9723942:

  • selected is unmodified master.

  • force_mmq has that final fall-through changed to return ne11 <= 1;, so MMQ from 2 columns up. One line, nothing else.

  • null_rebuild is byte-identical source to selected, just configured and built a second time. I wanted a noise floor before believing anything.

A10 at 150 W, driver 580.126.09, CUDA 12.8.93, clocks pinned with nvidia-smi -lgc 990, Llama-3.1-8B requantized with llama-quantize --pure --allow-requantize to Q4_0. Six rounds, rotating which binary goes first each round.

llama-bench -m pure_Q4_0.gguf -ngl 999 -fa 1 -p 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8 -n 0 -embd 1 -r 50
ne11selectedforce_mmqnull_rebuildforce_mmq / selected
195.5795.6295.551.0002
2179.17113.98179.030.6362
3260.03170.24259.830.6548
4306.68226.14306.590.7375
5358.03279.48358.010.7812
6377.42334.26377.310.8859
7389.41388.45390.600.9979
8406.10442.56406.371.0909
Two things about this table that I think make it trustworthy. At ne11 = 1 both binaries run the same code, because the change only affects ne11 >= 2, and the ratio comes out 1.0002. So there's a calibration point inside the experiment. And the null_rebuild factor, paired round by round, sits between 0.9991 and 1.0005 across all eight sizes, which puts the 9.1% at roughly a hundred times the noise floor. Dividing the two columns in the table instead gives 0.31% at ne11 = 7, because that picks up between-round drift the pairing removes; even on that looser measure the effect is about 30x the floor. The other thing worth saying is that force_mmq uses ne11 <= 1, but a cutoff of 7 would route identically at ne11 = 8, and wouldn't change anything at all below that. So that bottom row is a direct measurement of the change I'm suggesting, and I don't need a fourth binary to check it. (-embd 1 so the output projection is in there too, and the default ubatch of 512 means no splitting.) Why only 9.1% I also swept the individual matmul shapes with test-backend-ops perf, and the crossover turns out to depend a lot on the shape. For Llama-3.1-8B the four projection types don't agree with each other:
projectionm, kfirst ne11 where MMQ wins
down_proj4096, 143366
gate/up_proj14336, 40967
q_proj, o_proj4096, 40968
k/v_proj1024, 4096never, through 8

One cutoff has to cover all of those, and whole-model throughput is the weighted average, so a 27.6% per-kernel loss on down_proj comes out as 9.1% end to end. That's also why the net crossover lands on 8 rather than 6.

There's a bigger point buried in that table, which is that the crossover moves with the reduction dimension and a table keyed on typ

items.title: [Bug] FlashInfer autotune cache is discarded every boot under MoE expert parallelism (EP>1): per-rank shapes never agree, so the fused-MoE tactic is re-drawn each start
items.author: ntxf31415
items.body_excerpt:
### Summary

`_drop_diverged_autotune_cache()` discards the whole FlashInfer autotune cache — on every boot — whenever the per-rank MoE GEMM shapes differ, which is the normal case with **expert parallelism (EP > 1)**. The cache is then re-tuned from scratch each start, so the fused-MoE tactic is re-drawn every boot. Since the tactic selection is timing-based, end-to-end throughput varies across boots with identical config.

### Environment

- 4× GB10 (DGX Spark), SGLang TP4 / EP2, switchless RoCE ring
- MoE runner backend `flashinfer_mxfp4` (MXFP4 experts), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
- `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`, `--mem-fraction-static 0.90`
- FlashInfer 0.6.18, CUDA 13.0, cuDNN 92000

### Root cause

`python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/flashinfer_autotune.py`:

```python
def _autotune_cache_digest(cache_path, env):
    ...
    payload = {"file": configs, "env": env}
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()

def _drop_diverged_autotune_cache(cache_path, group, env) -> None:
    digests = [""] * torch.distributed.get_world_size(group)
    torch.distributed.all_gather_object(digests, _autotune_cache_digest(cache_path, env), group=group)
    if len(set(digests)) == 1:
        return
    ...
    cache_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)          # <-- deletes the cache
```

Each rank digests **its own** `rank_tp{N}_pp0_dp0.json` and all four are compared. Under EP sharding each rank owns a different slice of the routed experts, so **the MoE GEMM problem shapes themselves differ per rank** and the files can never be equal. Measured on our four ranks (same boot, same config, caches cleared so all four start from empty):

| rank | distinct shapes in its cache | example expert shape present |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 24 | `(192, 2304, 320)` |
| 1 | 24 | `(64, 2304, 320)` |
| 2 | 24 | `(64, 2304, 320)` / `(192, …)` |
| 3 | 24 | `(16, 5120)`, `(4, 5120)` |

**The intersection of the four shape sets is empty.** So `len(set(digests)) == 1` is never true, the cache is `unlink`ed on every start, and every start re-profiles `trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1` / `gemm2` for all shapes.

Startup log, one boot:

```
Running FlashInfer autotune with cache: /root/.cache/sglang/flashinfer/autotune/0.6.18/sm121/<key>/rank_tp3_pp0_dp0.json
[AutoTuner]: Tuning trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1:   0%|          | 0/8 ...
```

Tuning count is **26–27 profiles per boot** regardless of whether a complete cache file is already present at that path. The shipped image cache contains only `sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4` entries, so the fused-MoE shapes always miss anyway.

Note the digest also includes the environment, so even equal tactics would not be enough — but here the file contents themselves cannot match.

### Impact

The fused-MoE tactic is re-drawn on every start, and it matters a lot. Two consecutive boots of the same configuration, measured with a cold single-stream prefill probe at 8K tokens:

| boot | prefill t/s (8K) |
|---|---|
| A | 3169 |
| B | 2431 |

**−23 % at 8K**, while 100K was essentially unchanged (3266 vs 3164) — i.e. the draw is shape-range dependent, and a bad draw is stable for the whole life of that process. We also saw a full 1.5× swing on longer inputs between boots.

### Workaround we run

We mount a site-patched copy of this file that keeps the digest check and the log line but drops the `unlink`:

```python
    log_info_on_rank0(logger, "[site patch] keeping per-rank autotune caches")
```

With the per-rank caches kept, subsequent boots report **0 tuning profiles** (cache genuinely read and used) and throughput is stable.

⚠️ Caveat we found the hard way: this is only safe if every rank's own cache is **complete**. If some ranks hit and others miss, the missing ranks enter the timing-reduction collective while the others don't — we reproduced that as an NCCL collective timeout at startup with the process hanging, so a partial cache is worse than none.

### Possible fix directions

1. Compare like-for-like per rank (i.e. make the guard per-rank rather than requiring cross-rank equality), given that under EP the shape sets legitimately differ.
2. Or key the digest only on the *tactics for the shapes this rank actually uses*, rather than on the whole file.
3. Or make the reduction group follow the ranks that actually share a shape set.

If the divergence check is load-bearing for a reason we have not understood, it may be worth at least not deleting — logging and continuing — so a partially-cached fleet degrades to slow rather than to a hang.

items.title: [MegaMoE] W4A4 (mxf4xmxf4) target path for Kimi-K3: feature-completion patches + bs=1 perf/numerics findings
items.author: ZhimaoL
items.body_excerpt:
**What.** `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe` with mxfp4 quant selects `MmaKind::MXFP4` via `_mega_moe_mma_type()`, but (a) DeepGEMM's dev gate rejects MXFP4 for situ epilogues, and (b) `_forward_mega_experts` only implements the fp8 pre-dispatch — so K3 x W4A4 megamoe cannot serve today. We wrote the two small patches that complete the matrix and have been running them on 8xB300 (SM103), TP8, Kimi-K3 mxfp4:

1. DeepGEMM: admit `MmaKind::MXFP4` for situ (dev-gate relaxation; K3's `<9600,1792>` packed-fp4 geometry passes the existing shape checks; `kUseSitu` is mma-kind-agnostic; NVFP4 stays gated). → sgl-project/DeepGEMM#100
2. sglang: port the mxf4 branch `mega_moe.py` already carries into `kimi_k3.py::_forward_mega_experts` (+27/−10, `mma_type='mxf4xmxf4'`). → #43295

**With the pair applied, K3 W4A4 megamoe serves:** accept 3.170, step 40.24 ms at bs=1; re-reproduced in both patched-arm sessions of the evidence batch (2 fresh patched serves; 4 sessions total across arms).

**Findings maintainers should know (why this is feature-completion, not a perf PR):**
- bs=1 decode step is ~40 ms for BOTH W4A8 (41.77) and W4A4 (40.24) on v0.5.21-era builds — the whole-grid clustered launch + symm-ring cost appears to dominate at small token counts (math kind is not the wall; sgl-project/DeepGEMM#97's `global_num_tokens` tile hint does not change launch structure). Measured on image sha b1259f3e.
- Greedy prefix-equivalence vs the unpatched flashinfer_mxfp4 baseline diverges early on this vintage (prefix-match 0.145 W4A8 / 0.071 W4A4 vs baseline self-match ~1.0) — **task accuracy is nonetheless intact** (table below), consistent with benign numeric/order differences rather than quality loss, but we would appreciate maintainer eyes on whether this reproduces on HEAD (possibly related: #42812, #40751).
- Evidence batch (GSM8K 1319-q A/B x2, greedy, per the #42022 template):

| arm | run 1 | run 2 | pooled |
|---|---|---|---|
| patched (W4A4 megamoe, this PR pair) | 0.9788 (1291/1319) | 0.9750 (1286/1319) | **0.9769** |
| stock (flashinfer_mxfp4) | 0.9742 (1285/1319) | 0.9742 (1285/1319) | **0.9742** |

Pooled delta **+0.27%**; request errors 0/0 both arms; greedy (temperature 0), official 1319-question
test set, identical server/image/draft config both arms, fresh serve session per run.
**Pre-registered pass criterion (set before the run):** pooled |Δacc| ≤ 1.2% absolute (≈2σ at n=2×1319)
and |error-count Δ| ≤ 1% → pass.

Patches, raw GSM8K outputs, runner, serve command, and provenance: https://gist.github.com/ZhimaoL/aec832cf92f62f374e90936603fe3259
Happy to carry review feedback.

items.title: Same-type fp8 arithmetic passes the frontend and fails in LLVM lowering
items.author: LiRunGuo
items.body_excerpt:
`computation_type_impl` returns the fp8 type itself for same-type fp8 operands (rule added in #4222 so `tl.where` works on fp8, and asserted in `test_fp8_div_mod_promotion`: `(x * y).dtype == tl.float8e5`). But no backend can lower fp8 arithmetic, so `+ - *`, unary `-`, comparisons, `x * 2`, and `tl.sum` on an fp8 tensor all fail late with a verifier error instead of a frontend diagnostic:

```python
@triton.jit
def kernel(X, Y):
    offs = tl.arange(0, 128)
    x = tl.load(X + offs)          # *fp8e4nv
    tl.store(Y + offs, x * 2)
```
```
error: 'llvm.fmul' op operand #0 must be floating point LLVM type ..., but got 'i8'
RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed
```

Same on sm90/sm100 and gfx942/gfx950. `tl.maximum`, `tl.abs`, `tl.where`, `/` (promoted to fp32) work. Before #4222 this was a frontend `TypeError` (#2640, where fp8 arithmetic was described as expected-unsupported).

Options: (a) raise a clear frontend error for arithmetic/comparison on same-type fp8 while keeping selection ops (`where`, `maximum`, ...) fp8, or (b) promote same-type fp8 to fp16 like mixed fp8 already does (dtype-visible change). Happy to send whichever is preferred.

items.title: tl.dot_scaled in a loop: TritonGPUOptimizeAccumulatorInit PassManager::run failed on a non-carried accumulator
items.author: dkarpman
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

`TritonGPUOptimizeAccumulatorInit` aborts (`PassManager::run failed`) on a loop body whose `tl.dot_scaled` result is **not carried by a reassigned accumulator variable** — i.e. a fresh result tensor is bound each iteration. Every *reassigned-carried* accumulator form (the `acc=` argument, `acc += ...`, or a reset-per-iteration) compiles at all shapes tested.

This blocks `tl.dot_scaled` (mxfp4) kernels authored as a plain loop (the natural DeepGEMM-style persistent/tiled form).

### Reproducer (minimal, standalone)

```python
import torch, triton, triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def _loop_dot_scaled(lhs, lhs_sf, rhs, rhs_sf, out, NBLK: tl.constexpr):
    rn = tl.arange(0, 128); rk2 = tl.arange(0, 64); rs = tl.arange(0, 4)
    for blk in tl.range(0, NBLK, num_stages=2):
        off = blk * 128
        a = tl.load(lhs + (off + rn)[:, None] * 64 + rk2[None, :]).to(tl.uint8)
        a_sf = tl.load(lhs_sf + (off + rn)[:, None] * 4 + rs[None, :])
        b = tl.load(rhs + rk2[:, None] * 64 * NBLK + (off + rn)[None, :]).to(tl.uint8)
        b_sf = tl.load(rhs_sf + (off + rn)[:, None] * 4 + rs[None, :])
        acc = tl.dot_scaled(a, a_sf, "e2m1", b, b_sf, "e2m1", out_dtype=tl.float32)
        tl.store(out + (off + rn)[:, None] * 128 + rn[None, :], acc)
```

Launch with NBLK=8 on an sm100 device against zero-initialized uint8 operands shaped `(NBLK*128, 64)` / `(NBLK*128, 4)` (LHS), `(64, NBLK*128)` / `(NBLK*128, 4)` (RHS), fp32 out `(NBLK*128, 128)`.

Expected: compiles and runs. Actual:

```
error: Failures have been detected while processing an MLIR pass pipeline
note: Pipeline failed while executing [`TritonGPUOptimizeAccumulatorInit` on 'builtin.module' operation]
RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed
```

### What compiles vs crashes (measured)

| form | carrier | result |
|---|---|---|
| fresh per-iter `acc = tl.dot_scaled(...)`, loop-invariant operands | none | CRASH |
| fresh per-iter `acc = ...`, fresh operand loads per iter | none | CRASH |
| fresh per-iter `acc = ...`, MMA-N = 64 | none | CRASH |
| loop-invariant `zacc` passed as `acc=zacc` (never reassigned) | `acc=` (invariant) | CRASH |
| `acc += tl.dot_scaled(...)` (reassigned) | `+=` | OK |
| `acc = tl.dot_scaled(..., acc=acc)` (reassigned) | `acc=` | OK |
| `acc = acc * 0.0; acc = tl.dot_scaled(..., acc=acc)` (reassigned) | `acc=` | OK |
| nested: outer tile loop, inner carried-acc `tl.range(num_stages=2)` | `acc=` (reassigned) | OK |
| `tl.static_range` full unroll with fresh per-iter acc | n/a | OK |

The trigger is the non-reassigned result: it is independent of the MMA shape and the pipeline depth (also crashes with `num_stages=1` and a plain Python `range`).

### Environment

- Triton: 3.8.0
- GPU: NVIDIA B200 (sm100), CUDA 13.3
- Relevant pass: `lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/OptimizeAccumulatorInit.cpp`

items.title: [RFC] Review MC_USE_TENT=1 gaps for classic TE callers
items.author: staryxchen
items.body_excerpt:
## How this list was produced

Started as a static pass over:

- the C++ shim (`mooncake-transfer-engine/src/transfer_engine.cpp`, `use_tent_` branches)
- the Python wrapper (`mooncake-integration/transfer_engine/transfer_engine_py.cpp`)
- inference-engine call sites that use `mooncake.engine.TransferEngine`

Local runtime (2026-09-10, installed TENT wheel, 1P1D PD) then confirmed
some items and left others unverified. Status below is as of **2026-09-17**
(`origin/main` `c4d632888b`). Please still reproduce on your tree before
treating a remaining item as confirmed.

## Why the compatibility layer

We are wiring inference engines to TENT's **native** APIs, but that work is
not finished. Until it is, we use the classic TE compatibility layer
(`MC_USE_TENT=1`) to validate TENT **runtime** stability against existing
callers (PD disaggregation and others). This RFC tracks gaps in that layer.
It is not the native-API migration itself.

## Summary

`MC_USE_TENT=1` (and `MC_USE_TEV1=1`) is meant to run existing
`mooncake::TransferEngine` / `mooncake.engine.TransferEngine` code on the TENT
runtime. Register + sync submit/poll are wired up enough for PD KV transfer.

PD happy path **works** under `MC_USE_TENT=1` (local 1P1D Qwen3-4B
`/generate` 200). This RFC is not a claim that PD is broken today.

Most of the original P0/P1/P2 shim holes now have merged PRs. What is still
open is protocol pinning for `efa`/`ascend`, Python sync/poll semantics, and
`installTransport()` returning `nullptr` for classic C/Go/EFA callers.

If you find a **new** compatibility-layer issue, please report it on this
issue. We will add it to the work-item list.

## Non-goals

- Landing inference-engine (or Mooncake Store) native-API migration in this RFC
  (that work is separate and in progress, e.g. #4070).
- Teaching applications to `installTransport` under TENT. Making the shim
  honor the classic `Transport*` contract so existing callers do not treat a
  successful TENT init as failure **is** in scope (`P1-install-transport`).
- Changing TENT runtime scheduling / failover policy.

## Work items

Priority is "if the reading holds, impact is high" — not "already on fire".

| ID | Problem | Difficulty | PR | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P0-send_probe | Python `send_probe` SIGSEGV (`getMetadata()` is null) | M | #4081, follow-up #4115 | **done** |
| P0-stale-handle | Transfer failure may keep a dead peer's cached handle (`CheckSegmentStatus` was always OK) | M | #4109 | **partial** |
| P0-device-filter | `initialize(device=...)` still opened all HCAs | M | #4028 | **done** |
| P0-force-tcp | `MC_FORCE_TCP=1` / `protocol=tcp` may still select RDMA | M | #4027, follow-up #4113 | **done** |
| P0-efa-ascend | `protocol=efa\|ascend` may no-op or look successful without that transport | H | — | **open** |
| P1-sync-status | Python `transferSync` retry / `CANCELED` handling may not match TENT failover | S–M | — | **open** |
| P1-error-codes | Shim returned TENT `Status::Code` (non-negative); classic callers expect `ERR_*` | M | #4139 | **done** |
| P1-request-options | `priority` / `remote_accessible` were dropped at the shim | M | #4114 | **done** |
| P2-first-buffer | `getFirstBufferAddress` also called `getMetadata()` (same null deref as `send_probe`) | S | #4138 | **done** |
| P1-install-transport | TENT `installTransport()` returns `nullptr`; classic C/Go/EFA callers treat that as install failure | M | — | **open** |

### Residuals on landed items

These do not reopen the row, but they are not "the original hole is gone with no leftover":

- **P0-send_probe.** Python no longer dereferences `getMetadata()`. #4081 closed the segment after probing, which invalidated a handle already stored in Python `handle_map_`; #4115 stopped closing it. C++ `getMetadata()` is still `nullptr` under TENT — any remaining `getMetadata()->sendProbe` caller will still crash.
- **P0-stale-handle.** `CheckSegmentStatus` now probes via `probePeerAliveByID`. Python only calls it when **`submitTransfer` fails**. Peer death that shows up as `getTransferStatus` `FAILED` / `TIMEOUT` still leaves `handle_map_` intact. That leftover belongs with **P1-sync-status**. The unit test covers an never-opened handle, not a still-mapped handle whose RPC probe fails.
- **P0-force-tcp.** #4113 makes `forceTcp()` disable HP TCP so a config with both enabled does not fail init.
- **P1-error-codes.** Integer-returning APIs go through `tentToClassicError()`. `submitTransfer` still wraps TENT failures as `Status::Context(...)`. No in-tree test that failed on main and passed after (#4139 checklist).
- **P1-request-options.** Shim forwards `remote_accessible` → TENT perms and `TransferRequest::priority` on submit. Python `transferSync` does not set `priority` (default MEDIUM). No in-tree red/green test (#4114 checklist).

### Still open

- **P0-efa-ascend.** `init(..., protocol)` is now forwarded, but the TENT branch only special-cases `"tcp"`. `"efa"` / `"ascend"` do not pin those transports. On `USE_EFA` / `USE_CXI` Python builds, `initialize` still calls `installTransport()` after init; under TENT that returns `nullptr` and `initialize` returns `-1`. #4122 is classic TE Ascend Direct selection, not this shim item.
- **P1-sync-status.** `transferSync` still retries `numContexts()+1` times; under TENT `numContexts()` is hardcoded `1`. The poll loop handles `COMPLETED` / `FAILED` / `TIMEOUT` only — not `CANCELED` — and does not evict the cached handle on poll failure.
- **P1-install-transport.** Added from @chlins (2026-09-14). The TENT branch logs `"installTransport not used by TENT"` and returns `nullptr`. Classic contract: `nullptr` means install failed. Store already skips this via `isUsingTent()` (#2596). C / Go (`transfer_engine_c.h`) and EFA/CXI Python do not. Proposed fix A (TENT returns a non-null sentinel; in-tree callers only null-check) is preferred over gating every caller (B) or fixing only the C shim (C). Waiting on TENT owners (@alogfans) before a PR. R

## Changes proposed

Enable applications to select different Ascend transfer priorities within one process. Each priority lane owns an independently configured engine, allowing requests to select a lane without changing process-wide environment variables.

Proposed changes:

- Add explicit per-engine Ascend resource configuration through a six-argument `TransferEngine::init` overload and a corresponding Python initialization API. Preserve existing four- and five-argument calls.
- Preserve explicit per-engine resource overrides when loading TENT configuration.
- Provide Python priority-lane helpers for Store and PD transfers, including memory registration, failure cleanup, and engine lifecycle management.
- Keep Store lanes in a shared key space while retaining existing tenant, device, and replica settings.

This provides the backend for request-level KV transfer priority in vLLM-Ascend. Independently configured engines allow priorities to coexist while reusing the existing Ascend transport implementation.

Validation includes 22 CPU configuration tests, two initialization tests, one Store TCP test, TENT ON / Ascend Direct ON builds, native import and clean-exit probes, and A5 Store, PD, and layerwise integration tests.

Feedback is welcome on the per-engine initialization API and the placement of reusable priority-lane helpers in the Python package.

items.title: [Feature Request] Make Inductor benchmark GPU device-type selection accelerator-agnostic (third-party devices)
items.author: dingsheng758
items.body_excerpt:
### Context

`Inductor`'s autotuning benchmark must pick an available GPU device type to run candidate kernels on. That selection lives in `_get_default_gpu_device_type()` in `torch/_inductor/runtime/benchmarking.py`, and today it is backed by a hardcoded whitelist:

```python
GPU_BENCHMARK_DEVICE_TYPES = ("cuda", "xpu", "mtia")

def _get_default_gpu_device_type() -> str:
    avail_gpus = [
        device_type
        for device_type in GPU_BENCHMARK_DEVICE_TYPES
        if getattr(torch, device_type).is_available()
    ]
    if len(avail_gpus) > 1:
        raise AssertionError(
            f"expected at most one available GPU type, got {avail_gpus}"
        )
    return "cuda" if len(avail_gpus) == 0 else avail_gpus.pop()
```

Three problems with the status quo:

1. **Out-of-tree accelerators are invisible.** PrivateUse1 backends are not in the whitelist. On a host where only such a backend is available, `avail_gpus` is empty and the fallback returns `"cuda"` — benchmarking then targets a device that is not actually available.
2. **Multi-GPU-type hosts raise.** If a host has more than one GPU-class backend (e.g. cuda + xpu), the code raises `AssertionError: expected at most one available GPU type` instead of choosing one.
3. **It diverges from the rest of Inductor.** The rest of the stack classifies a GPU-class device via `torch._inductor.utils.get_gpu_type()` (`DeviceInterface.is_gpu()`), so the benchmark path and every other `get_gpu_type()` caller can disagree about which device is the GPU.

This issue was requested during review of the PR, where the reviewer asked that the issue be marked actionable before the PR proceeds. The change is open as #199806.

### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

**Blocker — the static whitelist above.**

**Pitch — one small change:** make `_get_default_gpu_device_type()` a thin delegate to `torch._inductor.utils.get_gpu_type()` (#199806). That helper:

- enumerates GPU-class backends through `DeviceInterface.is_gpu()` over `get_registered_device_interfaces()`;
- filters them to the ones actually available on the host, tolerating `NotImplementedError` from partially implemented out-of-tree interfaces via `_device_is_available()`;
- resolves a single device type via `torch.accelerator.current_accelerator()`, with a stable `"cuda"` fallback when several GPU types are present.

Because discovery builds on the shared `DeviceInterface` registry, any GPU-class backend that registers a `DeviceInterface` (`is_gpu()` returns `True`) is picked up automatically — out-of-tree PrivateUse1 backends need no benchmark-specific registration step. `cuda`/`xpu`/`mtia` behavior is unchanged.

**Request:** mark this actionable (or point us at the preferred design) so #199806 can proceed. Happy to implement a different shape.

### Alternatives

- **Status quo — per-backend static whitelist:** append each new accelerator's device type one by one. Every new backend needs a core patch, and multi-GPU-type hosts still raise.

### Additional context — expected behavior and testing

- Test added in the PR: `python -m pytest test/inductor/test_benchmarking.py::TestGpuBenchmarkDeviceTypes -x -q`
- Expected behavior (to be confirmed on real hardware):

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cuda-only host | `"cuda"` | `"cuda"` (unchanged) |
| host where only an out-of-tree PrivateUse1 backend is available | `"cuda"` (unavailable) | resolved to the registered device type |
| host with cuda + xpu | `AssertionError` | resolved via `current_accelerator()`, `"cuda"` fallback |

items.title: [Bug] GLM-5.3-Flash (DSA): HiCache host-tier load-back corrupts generation even without speculative decoding — dropped tool calls, degenerate repetition loops (8×H100, TP8)
items.author: d3lavar
items.body_excerpt:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

On GLM-5.3-Flash (packed DSA KV / `DSATokenToKVPool`, `--attention-backend dsa`), enabling HiCache host offload (`--hicache-size` / `--hicache-ratio`) corrupts generation for requests whose prefix round-trips through the host tier (device → host → device). **Speculative decoding is not required — the corruption reproduces with EAGLE/MTP fully disabled; HiCache alone is broken.** Three failure signatures, all appearing only after host load-back:

1. **Tool calls silently dropped** — `finish_reason=stop`, `tool_calls=null`, with a prose "answer" that often hallucinates the tool output, even though the model's reasoning explicitly announces the call.
2. **Degenerate repetition loops / broken token sequences** — output gets stuck repeating filler tokens from the system prompt (or a single phrase) until `max_tokens` truncation.

**Isolation on the same production 8×H100 node, same workload (2026-09-04):**

| HiCache (`--hicache-ratio 2 --hicache-size 140`) | EAGLE/MTP | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ON | ON | **corrupted** — signatures 1–3 |
| ON | **OFF** | **still corrupted** — intermittent: byte-identical warm replays mostly pass, but individual host load-back runs drop tool calls or loop (1 of 6 warm replays broken in one window, 4/4 post-eviction replays broken in another) |
| OFF (device radix only) | ON | clean — 5/5 on the originally broken session |

The corruption is **intermittent** on host load-back: a byte-identical replay succeeds several times in a row, then a later identical replay corrupts (see `warm1/warm2/warm3` below). The fault lives in the **HiCache host-tier load-back path itself**; EAGLE adds its own draft-state sensitivity on top (#28895) but is not required for the bug.

### Setup

- **Hardware:** 8× NVIDIA H100 (single node), TP8 / DP1 / EP8
- **Image:** [`lmsysorg/sglang:glm-5.3-flash`](https://hub.docker.com/r/lmsysorg/sglang) — build of PR #36507 (branch `xinyuan/glm-5.3-flash-support`), with #37925 (`glm53` tool-call parser) and #37534 (packed-DSA HiCache host-row width fix) cherry-picked. The corruption persists with both, so #37534 is not sufficient for the spec-decode combination.
- **Launch (broken config), flags confirmed verbatim from `/server_info`:**

  ```bash
  python -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path glm-5.3-flash \
    --tp-size 8 --dp-size 1 --ep-size 8 \
    --attention-backend dsa \
    --page-size 64 \
    --tool-call-parser glm53 --reasoning-parser glm45 \
    --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 16384 \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.7 --max-running-requests 48 \
    --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
    --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
    --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 --speculative-adaptive \
    --hicache-ratio 2 --hicache-size 140 \
    --hicache-write-policy write_through \
    --hicache-mem-layout page-first-direct \
    --hicache-io-backend direct
  ```

  Removing the `--hicache-*` flags removes the corruption. Disabling EAGLE does **not** — with HiCache on, generation still corrupts without speculative decoding but later, cannot determine the moment yet.
- **Pressure conditions:** device KV pool ~93% used (~601K tokens), host pool LRU ~99.9% full — prefixes actively evict to host and load back between turns.
- **Workload:** agentic client, 47 tools, streaming, OpenAI-style history, 100K–230K-token prompts.

### Evidence (verbatim excerpts from the script above, HiCache ON, glm53 parser + #37534 build; observed with EAGLE both ON and OFF)

Phase 1 (device radix hits) is mostly healthy, but even the first warm window already drops calls intermittently:

```text
cold-180K    dt=27.3s  prompt=225686  cached=128     finish=tool_calls  tools=['bash']
warm1-180K   dt= 1.7s  prompt=225686  cached=225664  finish=tool_calls  tools=['bash']
warm2-180K   dt= 1.1s  prompt=225686  cached=225664  finish=stop        tools=[]      <- BROKEN
warm3-180K   dt= 1.5s  prompt=225686  cached=225664  finish=tool_calls  tools=['bash']
```

`warm2-180K` content — the model hallucinates the tool result instead of calling the tool:

```text
Here's the output from running the command:

```
hello-acceptance
```
```

Phase 3 (same byte-identical prompts after eviction, i.e. served from HiCache host load-back) — tool-call drops plus degenerate repetition loops:

```text
replay1-60K   dt= 0.8s  cached=75328   finish=stop          tools=[]  tail: "echo hello-acceptance"
replay2-60K   dt=33.0s  cached=75328   finish=length(2000)  tools=[]  tail: "oscar oscar oscar oscar oscar oscar 999999999
juliet juliet juliet jul"
replay1-180K  dt=28.0s  cached=225664  finish=length(2000)  tools=[]  tail: "tice the notice the notice the notice the notice ..."
replay2-180K  dt=58.2s  cached=225664  finish=length(2000)  tools=[]
```

`oscar`/`juliet` are random filler words from the system prompt — the model is regurgitating corrupted prefill tokens. Phase 2 (eviction pressure, ~2.2M tokens vs ~601K device pool)

For comparison: with HiCache disabled (device radix only) — clean, including warm replays and post-eviction replays; with EAGLE disabled but HiCache on — corruption is still observed on host load-back (tool-call drops and repetition loops, as above).

### Notes on root cause (hypothesis)

Host-tier backup/load-back corrupts the packed DSA KV rows themselves (`DSATokenToKVPool`): after a device → host → device round-trip the prefill KV no longer matches what the original token sequence produced, so the model "misreads its own history" — no valid tool call, confabulated r

items.title: [FX][Performance] Expensive repeated cycle checks in CapabilityBasedPartitioner.propose_partitions()
items.author: lqx2005
items.body_excerpt:
## report

The submitter specified the problem framing and scope. The technical analysis and code were drafted by an AI assistant under the submitter's direction. Test results and environment information were collected through actual tool executions and summarized by the assistant.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Repeated cycle checks in `CapabilityBasedPartitioner.propose_partitions()`
cause high partitioning overhead on large FX graphs. Partitioning results
are correct; the issue is compilation time.

### Motivation

While working with SDXL UNet, partitioning a graph with 9,672 FX nodes became a compilation bottleneck. `propose_partitions()` operated on the entire FX graph before Inductor IR lowering, so `ComputedBuffer` objects were not present at this stage.

Repeated dependency scans across this large graph make candidate cycle checks expensive. The goal is to reduce this overhead while preserving the existing fusion decisions.

### Minimal reproducer (AI-generated code)

This CPU-only example constructs the chain `input -> neg -> relu -> neg -> relu -> ... -> output`. The support predicate accepts `neg` and rejects `relu`, so merging any two supported partitions would create a cycle through an unsupported node. The expected and actual result is one partition per `neg`. Only PyTorch is required; no tensor operations are executed.

```python
import cProfile
import statistics
import time

import torch
from torch.fx import Graph, GraphModule
from torch.fx.passes.infra.partitioner import CapabilityBasedPartitioner
from torch.fx.passes.operator_support import OperatorSupportBase


class Support(OperatorSupportBase):
    def is_node_supported(self, submodules, node):
        return node.op == "call_function" and node.target is torch.neg


def make_graph(n):
    graph = Graph()
    x = graph.placeholder("x")
    for _ in range(n):
        x = graph.call_function(torch.neg, (x,))
        x = graph.call_function(torch.relu, (x,))
    graph.output(x)
    return GraphModule(torch.nn.Module(), graph)


for n in (64, 128, 256):
    gm = make_graph(n)
    durations = []

    for _ in range(3):
        partitioner = CapabilityBasedPartitioner(
            gm, Support(), allows_single_node_partition=True
        )
        start = time.perf_counter()
        partitions = partitioner.propose_partitions()
        durations.append(time.perf_counter() - start)

    # Count cycle checks separately to avoid profiling the timed runs.
    partitioner = CapabilityBasedPartitioner(
        gm, Support(), allows_single_node_partition=True
    )
    profiler = cProfile.Profile()
    profiler.runcall(partitioner.propose_partitions)
    checks = sum(
        entry.callcount
        for entry in profiler.getstats()
        if getattr(entry.code, "co_name", "") == "dfs_iter_find_cycle"
    )

    print(
        f"nodes={len(list(gm.graph.nodes))}, "
        f"partitions={len(partitions)}, "
        f"cycle_checks={checks}, "
        f"median_s={statistics.median(durations):.6f}"
    )
```

### Observed results (AI-run tests; AI-generated summary)

| FX nodes | Supported nodes | Cycle checks | Successful merges | propose_partitions() |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 130 | 64 | 4,032 | 0 | 0.020928 s |
| 258 | 128 | 16,256 | 0 | 0.118784 s |
| 514 | 256 | 65,280 | 0 | 0.826554 s |

Measured with the unmodified PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu partitioner. Times are medians of three unprofiled runs, excluding graph and partitioner construction. Counts come from separate profiling runs; this chain produces `n(n-1)` checks for `n` supported nodes.

### Worst-case upper bounds

Let `N` be the number of input FX nodes and `W = ceil(N / w)` the bitset width in words, with word width `w`. These are worst-case upper bounds for one invocation with `skip_horizontal_fusion=False`, assuming expected constant-time hash lookups. They cover cycle checks and accepted-merge updates, excluding unchanged candidate sorting and postprocessing.

| Operation | Original implementation | Differential bitset implementation |
|---|---|---|
| Successful merges | `O(N)` | `O(N)` |
| Cycle-check calls | `O(N^2)` | `O(N^2)` |
| One cycle check | `O(N^2)` | `O(W)` |
| Reachability maintenance after one accepted merge | `O(N^3)` | `O(NW)` |
| Combined cycle-checking and accepted-merge update work | `O(N^4)` | `O(N^2 W)` |

### Approach and scope

The original implementation scans cached downstream nodes for each external user of the candidate partitions. After a successful merge, it also unions reachable-partition sets while scanning those dependencies.

The replacement maintains exact ancestor and descendant bitsets of the current partition graph. It checks merges using bitset intersections and propagates only differences after an accepted merge. This makes frequent queries cheaper while updating reachability only after successful merges.

| Additional bitset cost | Worst-case bound |
|---|---|
| Initialization | `O(N^2 W)` |
| Reachability storage | `O(N^2)` bits, plus graph bookkeeping |

The change is limited to cycle detection and its dependency maintenance. Candidate generation and ordering, support predicates, horizontal-fusion policy, partition membership and ordering, `getitem` reassignment, and single-node filtering remain unchanged.

### Algorithm

The helper maintains the current partition graph: each vertex represents a
partition, and edges represent dependencies between partitions. Initially,
every FX node is a singleton, including nodes that are not fusion candidates.
For each live vertex `v`, it stores strict ancestors `A(v)` and strict
descendants `D(v)` as bitsets. Neither set includes `v` itself. Initialization
propagates ancestors in topological order and descendants in reverse order.

**Cycle check.** For distinct vertices `a` and `b` in the current DAG, reject
merging them exactly when:

```text
(D(a) & A(b)) | (D(b) & A(a)) != empty
```

items.title: [Testing] Triage of red tests that still need a fix (90-day sweep)
items.author: bolubo
items.body_excerpt:
## Summary

A 90 day sweep of the Actions history (2026-06-26 to 2026-09-25) turned up 455 failed runs. Most of them are already fixed, tied to a PR branch that was still iterating, or environmental. This issue is about what is left: tests that are still going red and do not have a fix, with enough evidence attached that someone can pick one up without redoing the whole investigation.

Two of the items reproduce locally on main today (A). Four more keep showing up in CI across branches, where the mechanism is narrowed down but there is no local repro yet (B). The appendices cover the one-off flakes and the families that are already fixed, so nobody has to dig through them again.

The coverage side already has tracking issues (#2637, #2708, #2737); this list is a different axis, tests that are failing right now.

If you want to take one, please comment on the item first so two people do not end up on the same thing, and link the PR here when it is up. Small focused PRs are the easiest to review.

## Items

- [ ] A1. Gateway rate limiter windows follow the wall clock, and three tests flake on the bucket boundary.
- [ ] A2. Two tests have been skipped since April 2025, and both pass when re-enabled.
- [ ] B1. The SLO queue spec times out on the release path.
- [ ] B2. The RoleSet topology spec hits a 409 conflict.
- [ ] B3. Batch e2e: a restored job does not reach `completed` within the 60s budget.
- [ ] B4. The planner unit test hangs and trips the 10 minute package timeout.

Grading:

- A: reproduced locally on main (`544204ae`), with a measured failure rate over repeated runs.
- B: repeated red in CI on main or across branches; no local repro yet.
- Watch: seen once; kept for reference.
- Fixed: already covered by a merged PR; do not re-triage.

## A. Reproduced locally on main

### A1. Gateway rate limiter windows follow the wall clock

`pkg/plugins/gateway/ratelimiter/redis.go:77` builds the counter key as `name:key:<unix/window % 64>`, so the counter changes on wall-clock bucket boundaries. A pair of calls that should share one window can land in two buckets instead, and the second call gets a fresh counter and is admitted. The TTL side is already anchored to the first write (`incrAndExpireScript`), so the key rotation is the remaining race.

- Affected tests: `pkg/plugins/gateway/replica_rps_test.go:96` (`TestModelReplicaRPS_Half_AllowsOneRequestEveryTwoSeconds`), `pkg/plugins/gateway/replica_inflight_test.go:335` (`TestHandleRequestBody_ReplicaInflightCoexistsWithReplicaRPS`), and `pkg/plugins/gateway/gateway_ratelimit_test.go:270` (`TestEnforceModelRPS_RejectDoesNotPostponeNextWindow`, added with #2726).
- How often it fails on main (one process per run, `-count=1`): 3 red in 100 runs for the first pair, 14 red in 450 runs for the third test, so roughly one run in thirty. The failure messages are "a second request within the same 2s window should be rejected" and "immediate retry should be rejected by the still-open window".
- CI hit: [run 35654425095, job 106514390571](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/actions/runs/35654425095/job/106514390571), Go Race Tests on 09-21, same assertion at `gateway_ratelimit_test.go:270`.
- Repro: `for i in $(seq 1 50); do go test ./pkg/plugins/gateway -run 'TestModelReplicaRPS_Half_AllowsOneRequestEveryTwoSeconds|TestHandleRequestBody_ReplicaInflightCoexistsWithReplicaRPS' -count=1; done`
- Two ways to fix it, and this is a real tradeoff: (1) anchor the window at the first write so every call in the same window computes the same key, which is what the tests already assume, at the cost of changing behavior at bucket boundaries; or (2) keep the wall-clock bucket and make the tests independent of it by injecting the clock, which is a smaller change but leaves the boundary burst in the product.

### A2. Two tests skipped since April 2025

- `pkg/utils/prefixcacheindexer/tree_test.go:33` (`Test_LPRadixCacheE2E`) and `:71` (`Test_RadixMatchPrefix`) have carried `t.SkipNow()` since `d546795a` (#933, April 2025). Removing the two lines makes both pass locally, in under 0.1s including subtests.
- `apps/console/api/resource_manager/provider/kubernetes/catalog_test.go:33` skips unconditionally with `t.Skip("skip for now")`, which also makes the kubeconfig checks below it dead code. Either delete the line or gate it on the environment with a stated reason.
- Repro: `go test ./pkg/utils/prefixcacheindexer -run 'Test_LPRadixCacheE2E|Test_RadixMatchPrefix' -v`

## B. Repeated red in CI, no local repro yet

### B1. SLO queue spec times out on the release path

- `pkg/plugins/gateway/algorithms/slo_test.go:253` ("Queue router should be blocked and released successfully") fails with `context deadline exceeded` at `:270`, after the 10s per spec budget.
- Hits since June: 06-28 `exclusive_topology`, 08-17 `route-dev` and `feat/align-job-time-window`, 09-05 `ui-aiconfigurator`, 09-09 `feat-pd-hybrid-cache-load`, 09-12 `roshpr/feat-stormservice-pooled-scale`, 09-20 `andreafeat/disable-gateway-rate-limiting` (race job). #2335 reported this spec in June and was closed after #2328 and #2353 merged, but it still recurs.
- A 150 run local loop is green, so it needs a CI style repro first. Fixing it likely means either making the assertion event driven or making the fixed wait budget explicit and generous.

### B2. RoleSet topology spec hits a 409 conflict

- `test/integration/controller/roleset_test.go:1062` ("applies topology policy updates only to newly created pods") fails at `:1118` with `Operation cannot be fulfilled on rolesets... the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again`. Latest hit: [35814726502](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/actions/runs/35814726502) on main, 09-23, 89 of 90 specs passed. Two more on 08-04.
- The spec updates the RoleSet while a reconcile is in flight, so `retry.RetryOnConflict` around the update (or `Eventually`) should close the race. Test side, no product change expected.

Looking at `test/integration/controller/roleset_test.go`, the spec "applies topology policy updates only to newly created pods" does a bare Get + mutate + `Update` on the RoleSet twice (`:1096` and `:1118` on current main). comments.author: hengguangcui11-cyber
comments.body:
I did some investigation on B1 and I think I found the root cause. It also explains why #2328 and #2353 didn't stop it from recurring. I'd like to take this one. cc @varungup90 since this builds on #2353.

**Root cause.** The failure at `slo_test.go:270` is a *fill* request timing out (`fillRequestTimeout` = 10s), not the request that is supposed to block. The fill loop sent one request too many.

#2353 added the second `AddRequestCount` call in `queueRouter.Route` (`queue_router.go:118`) so that `RealtimeNormalizedPendings` is updated before `Route()` returns. `CanAddStats()` guarantees that `addPodStats` runs exactly once, but not that it has *finished* when the other caller returns:

1. The `serve()` goroutine wins the CAS and enters `addPodStats`. It has not yet reached the pending-load update (`cache_trace.go:354-368`).
2. The requester wakes up, calls `AddRequestCount`, loses the CAS (`cache_impl.go:312`), and returns right away.
3. `Route()` returns while the pod's pending load still holds the previous value.

`waitForPendingLoadMetric` (`slo_test.go:66`) returns as soon as the metric *exists*, so after the first request it reads the stale value. The fill loop then thinks there's room for one more request, sends it, and that request exceeds the cap and is queued. Nothing releases it during the fill phase, so it waits out the full 10s and fails with `context deadline exceeded` at `:270`. That's also why the larger budgets in #2328 couldn't help: no timeout is long enough for a request that will never be dequeued.

**Why this isn't only a test problem.** The race goes both ways. If the requester wins the CAS instead, `serve()` is the one that loses. It returns from `AddRequestCount` in `routeNext` right away and goes on to route the next queued request. As far as I can tell, the SLO routers read that same `RealtimeNormalizedPendings` through `NewPendingLoadProvider`, so that next decision can see the pod's load without the request it just placed. That could briefly admit past the cap.

**Repro.** Like the issue says, it doesn't reproduce naturally on my machine either: 0 failures in 2000 runs with `-race` and all cores saturated. But widening the window makes it deterministic. With a 20ms sleep added in `addPodStats` right before the pending-load update, the spec fails every time at `:270` with `context deadline exceeded` after about 10s, which is the same signature as the CI runs listed above.

**Proposed fix (product side, completing what #2353 intended).**
- Add a channel to `RoutingContext` that the CAS winner closes (via `defer`) once `addPodStats` returns. The loser waits on it before returning, so the guarantee in the `queue_router.go` comment actually holds.
- Recreate the channel in `reset()`, since contexts come from `sync.Pool`. Closing it with `defer` covers `addPodStats`'s early returns (pod not found, no provider). If stats are already done, the channel is already closed and the wait is a no-op.
- Regression test in `pkg/cache` that doesn't need a hook in production code: a fake `pendingLoadProvider` whose `GetConsumption` blocks on a channel holds the winner inside that window. The test asserts that a second `AddRequestCount` doesn't return until the provider is released, and that the metric is already updated when it does.

Optionally, I can also make `waitForPendingLoadMetric` wait for the value to actually change instead of just existing. That alone would make this spec pass, but it wouldn't fix the `serve()`-side case above, so I'd rather do it in addition to the product fix than instead of it.

Let me know if you'd prefer the test-only route instead. Otherwise I'll open the PR along these lines.

comments.body:
I'd like to take B4.

In the goroutine dump from that run, `WorkerPool.Stop` is waiting on its WaitGroup, but no worker goroutine is left, so a task was counted and never ran. In the pool at that commit, `Submit` added to the WaitGroup, released the lock, and then picked between sending the task and `ctx.Done()`. `planningLoop.Stop` cancelled the context and stopped the pool while `planOnce` could still be submitting. If `Stop` drained the queue in between, the send could still win, and the task sat in the queue with no worker to run it. So the failed provision was incidental; any submit in flight during `Close` could do it.

#2634 already fixed this, since `Stop` now waits for in-flight `Submit` calls before draining, but nothing tests that race. I'll add a regression test for it. It hangs on the old pool within a few attempts and passes on main.

items.title: [Bug] KV event replay never applies the replayed batches
items.author: sohom-cs
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

`ZMQClient` asks the vLLM KV event publisher for a replay when it starts, from seq 0 ([zmq_client.go#L149](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/a26d827c0bbb0dd43079c7d7853a7bd32d89eb1e/pkg/cache/kvcache/zmq_client.go#L149)), and after every reconnect, from `lastSeq+1` ([#L251](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/a26d827c0bbb0dd43079c7d7853a7bd32d89eb1e/pkg/cache/kvcache/zmq_client.go#L251)). The replayed batches never reach the prefix index.

vLLM answers a replay request with one message per buffered batch and then an end marker with seq -1 ([`_service_replay`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/111f71a6dbf1fe517f6164e1059a2837bb0a8b4e/vllm/distributed/kv_events.py#L509-L527)). `requestReplay` reads a single frame ([#L394](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/a26d827c0bbb0dd43079c7d7853a7bd32d89eb1e/pkg/cache/kvcache/zmq_client.go#L394)), which is the empty delimiter of the first replayed message. It logs `Successfully requested replay from seq 0 for <pod> (response: 0 bytes)` and returns. The batches and the end marker stay unread in the DEALER socket.

What this breaks:

- A gateway that subscribes after the engine has cached blocks never indexes those blocks. Later `BlockStored` events whose parent is one of them are skipped as "unknown parent" ([sync_hash.go#L280-L287](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/a26d827c0bbb0dd43079c7d7853a7bd32d89eb1e/pkg/utils/syncprefixcacheindexer/sync_hash.go#L280-L287)), so prefixes that extend an earlier cached prefix are not indexed either.
- Events published while the client was disconnected are not recovered.
- The frames left in the socket are read by the next replay request as its response.

The unit tests did not catch it because the mock publisher answers a replay request with a single `"OK"` frame ([zmq_client_test.go#L635](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/a26d827c0bbb0dd43079c7d7853a7bd32d89eb1e/pkg/cache/kvcache/zmq_client_test.go#L635)).

A separate thing I noticed while reading this code, not part of this bug: the replay port is fixed at `DefaultRouterPort = 5558`, while `samples/semantic-router/models/qwen3-8b.yaml` publishes replay on 5559 and the vLLM P/D samples in `samples/disaggregation/vllm/` use 5558 for the NIXL side channel.

### Steps to Reproduce

A ROUTER that follows vLLM's replay protocol, plus the send and receive steps of `requestReplay` (pebbe/zmq4 v1.4.0, libzmq 4.3.5, Go 1.24):

```go
package main

import (
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"time"

	zmq "github.com/pebbe/zmq4"
)

func seqBytes(s int64) []byte { b := make([]byte, 8); binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(b, uint64(s)); return b }

func main() {
	router, _ := zmq.NewSocket(zmq.ROUTER)
	router.Bind("tcp://127.0.0.1:15558")
	// vLLM side: replay buffer holds batches seq 7..9
	go func() {
		frame, _ := router.RecvMessageBytes(0) // [client_id, "", start_seq]
		client := frame[0]
		start := int64(binary.BigEndian.Uint64(frame[2]))
		for s := int64(7); s <= 9; s++ {
			if s >= start {
				router.SendMessage(client, []byte{}, []byte("kv-events"), seqBytes(s), []byte(fmt.Sprintf("payload-%d", s)))
			}
		}
		router.SendMessage(client, []byte{}, []byte{}, seqBytes(-1), []byte{}) // END_SEQ
	}()
	dealer, _ := zmq.NewSocket(zmq.DEALER)
	dealer.Connect("tcp://127.0.0.1:15558")
	time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
	// same send/receive steps as aibrix requestReplay
	dealer.SendMessage([]byte{}, seqBytes(0))
	dealer.SetRcvtimeo(5 * time.Second)
	resp, err := dealer.RecvBytes(0)
	fmt.Printf("requestReplay returns: err=%v, response %d bytes (logged as success)\n", err, len(resp))
	// what is left unread in the DEALER queue
	time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond)
	n := 0
	for {
		parts, err := dealer.RecvMessageBytes(zmq.DONTWAIT)
		if err != nil {
			break
		}
		n++
		fmt.Printf("  unread message %d: %d frames, seq frame=%v\n", n, len(parts), parts[len(parts)-2])
	}
	fmt.Printf("replayed batches never decoded/applied: %d messages left in socket\n", n)
}
```

Output:

```
requestReplay returns: err=<nil>, response 0 bytes (logged as success)
  unread message 1: 3 frames, seq frame=[0 0 0 0 0 0 0 7]
  unread message 2: 4 frames, seq frame=[0 0 0 0 0 0 0 8]
  unread message 3: 4 frames, seq frame=[0 0 0 0 0 0 0 9]
  unread message 4: 4 frames, seq frame=[255 255 255 255 255 255 255 255]
replayed batches never decoded/applied: 4 messages left in socket
```

This uses the framing of vLLM v0.26 and later, `[empty, topic, seq, payload]`. vLLM v0.25 and earlier send `[empty, seq, payload]` (the topic frame was added in vllm-project/vllm#45177). The first frame is the empty delimiter in both, so the result is the same.

### Expected behavior

`requestReplay` reads replies until the end marker, applies each replayed batch newer than `lastSeq` the same way as live batches, and bounds the whole replay by `ReplayTimeout`. A reply that times out is not read as the answer to the next request.

I'm opening a PR with a fix and tests.

### Environment

- AIBrix: main at a26d827
- vLLM: any version started with a `replay_endpoint` in `--kv-events-config`. I checked the replay code in `vllm/distributed/kv_events.py` for v0.11.0 through v0.30.0; only the topic frame changed.
- Found by reading the code and reproduced with the program above, not in a cluster.

### Area

Gateway

items.title: [Bug] RoPE FP8 quantize trace references clamp e5m2 outputs at the e4m3 max of 448
items.author: GowayLee
items.body_excerpt:
## Environment

- flashinfer source tree at commit `a297b577c`, torch 2.9.0, CPU (the trace references are pure PyTorch)

## Bug description

The RoPE + FP8 quantize references in `flashinfer/trace/templates/rope.py` clamp every quantized value to the e4m3 range before the cast, regardless of the requested dtype.

```python
# flashinfer/trace/templates/rope.py, current main
def _q(t, scale):
    return (
        (t.to(torch.float32) * float(scale)).clamp(-448.0, 448.0).to(quantize_dtype)
    )
```

448 is the max of `float8_e4m3fn`. The `quantize_dtype` parameter accepts `float8_e5m2` across the whole API family. The public docstring of `rope_quantize_fp8` in `flashinfer/rope.py` reads "Must be `torch.float8_e4m3fn` or `torch.float8_e5m2`", and the TVM FFI binding at `csrc/rope.cu:310` whitelists both dtypes. An e5m2 request therefore has every magnitude above 448 clipped to the endpoint on both signs, while values below 448 pass through untouched. The e5m2 representable range is silently compressed by 128x (57344 / 448). The same constant clamp appears a second time in `_rope_quantize_fp8_append_paged_kv_cache_reference`, in the `v_q` branch that quantizes V before writing it into the paged `v_cache`.

The CUDA kernels already behave correctly here. `vec_dtypes.cuh` stores FP8 through `cvt.rn.satfinite.e4m3x2.f16x2` and `cvt.rn.satfinite.e5m2x2.f16x2`, which saturate each format at its own max, so for e5m2 the kernels agree with a ±57344 bound. The references are the side that disagrees, and the repository already carries the dtype-dispatched form in `flashinfer/triton/kernels/quant.py`, where `scale_and_clamp` maps e5m2 to ±57344. #4202 fixed the same construction in `rmsnorm_quant`, whose CUDA fallback clamped e5m2 outputs at 448 as well.

The disagreement has stayed invisible because the three reference correctness tests (`test_rope_quantize_fp8_reference_correctness.py`, `test_mla_rope_quantize_fp8_reference_correctness.py`, and the append paged KV one) never pass `quantize_dtype`, so the default e4m3fn path is the only one ever exercised.

### Measured impact

The numbers below come from CPU verification of the pinned reference code, which is byte-identical in current main.

- On a bf16-exact magnitude grid spanning the 448 neighborhood up past 57344 on both signs, 70.75% of in-domain elements (2400 of 3392) have their value changed. A seed=0 log-uniform random batch of 4096 values reaches 44.05%, and `quant_scale_q=4` pushes the same grid to 97.80%.
- The largest absolute deviation is 56896, the full span between 57344 and 448.
- The mismatch set equals the elementwise prediction `e5m2(clamp(v)) != e5m2(v)`, and every affected element has |v| > 448. The e4m3 control run changes zero elements, since 448 is the correct bound there.
- The append reference writes the same clamped values into `v_cache`, so a V value of 500 lands as 448 where the nearest e5m2 value is 512.

## Minimal reproduction

```python
import torch
from flashinfer.trace.templates.rope import rope_quantize_fp8_trace

# pos_ids 0 with cos 1 / sin 0 makes the rotation an identity, so the
# quantizer sees exactly the values below. All are exact in bf16.
cos_sin_cache = torch.tensor([[1.0, 0.0]], dtype=torch.float32)
pos_ids = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32)
q_rope = torch.tensor([[[57344.0, 2048.0]]], dtype=torch.bfloat16)
k_rope = torch.tensor([[[512.0, -59904.0]]], dtype=torch.bfloat16)
q_r, k_r, _, _ = rope_quantize_fp8_trace.reference(
    q_rope,
    k_rope,
    None,
    None,
    cos_sin_cache,
    pos_ids,
    quantize_dtype=torch.float8_e5m2,
)
print("reference  :", q_r.float().tolist(), k_r.float().tolist())
print("torch cast :", q_rope.to(torch.float8_e5m2).float().tolist(),
      k_rope.to(torch.float8_e5m2).float().tolist())
```

Output on current main.

```
reference  : [[[448.0, 448.0]]] [[[448.0, -448.0]]]
torch cast : [[[57344.0, 2048.0]]] [[[512.0, -57344.0]]]
```

The reference line clips 57344, 2048, and 512 down to 448 and lifts -59904 to -448, while the direct torch cast keeps every value inside the e5m2 range. With the fix attached to this issue the reference matches the torch cast line exactly.

## Additional context

The attached PR dispatches the clamp bounds on `quantize_dtype` through a module-level helper that maps e4m3fn to ±448, e5m2 to ±57344, and raises for anything else, mirroring the satfinite intrinsics and the triton `scale_and_clamp` table. Both call sites change and the e4m3 behavior is untouched. The regression tests are CPU-only, cover both reference entry points plus the unchanged e4m3 path, and fail on main for e5m2.

## 审查判断点（以下为内部材料，不随 issue 提交）

1. 范围只写 trace reference 两处。CUDA kernel、triton `scale_and_clamp`、binding 白名单都是正确侧，作为对照证据引用，不改。
2. "byte-identical in current main" 指 `flashinfer/trace/templates/rope.py` 自验证钉死点 `dd12b73b`（2026-09-09）至 `a297b577c` 零 diff，已用 fetch 后的 git 对象核实；正文不写内部 commit 语义之外的细节。
3. 影响数字四条全部来自 results.jsonl（grid 70.75%、random 44.05%、scale4 97.80%、max 56896、site2 的 500→448/512）。"quant_scale_q=4 pushes the same grid to 97.80%" 的口径是同网格加 scale（grid_scale4 行）。
4. e4m3 零改变的表述附带"since 448 is the correct bound there"，把对照结果与机制绑定，避免读者误读为修复的副作用。
5. #4202 引用是同仓相对号；如维护者问先例细节，rmsnorm 案的修复（QuantTypeStaticVals<O>::MAX_VAL dispatch）与本 PR 的 helper 分派同构。
6. 复现脚本在未修树与修复树各逐字跑过，输出行为实际执行结果；修复侧输出与 torch cast 行逐值一致。
7. 模板 outputs 声明（`Tensor(..., dtype="float8_e4m3fn")`）在 e5m2 请求下同样不匹配，属 trace schema 层的次生问题，牵动 template consistency 测试，未纳入本 PR；如需跟进可在 PR 讨论中提。

items.title: [Store] remove + re-put of the same key never re-offloads with the bucket backend
items.author: he-yufeng
items.body_excerpt:
While extending the regression coverage on #3889 I hit an offload quirk that looks worth its own report.

Repro, in-proc master harness with `bucket_storage_backend` and `MOONCAKE_OFFLOAD_BUCKET_KEYS_LIMIT=1`:

1. `put(key)` then the object offloads, LOCAL_DISK replica R1 registered.
2. `remove(key)`, master record erased.
3. `put(key)` again, fresh memory replica, PutEnd queues the offload task.
4. The next heartbeat takes the task but the key comes back as a NACK (`data_size=-1`) and no new disk replica ever registers. The object stays memory-only indefinitely.

What happens on the client: `FileStorage::OffloadObjects` finds the local slices fine, but `BucketStorageBackend` still holds the key in `object_bucket_map_` from the first offload (remove never reaches the backend), so `BatchOffload` skips it as an already-persisted duplicate without invoking the completion callback, and `FileStorage` NACKs it per the "a successful batch may skip duplicates" contract. The master erases the offload marker on the NACK, so the key can never be offloaded again until the backend evicts the stale entry.

Two consequences:

- Durability: a re-put object silently loses its disk tier. If the memory replica is later evicted the object is gone, even with free SSD capacity.
- Staleness: the backend map still points at the old bucket file with the old bytes. Nothing serves it while the master holds no disk record, but a rescan-based path (master restart + `ReRegisterOffloadedObjects`) looks like it could re-register the old bytes under the new object. I have not verified that second path end to end.

Possible directions: propagate `remove()` to the storage backend so the persisted entry drops with the master record, or let `BatchOffload` overwrite a persisted entry under a generation check instead of skipping it.

Observed on current main (ubuntu 22.04 container, gcc) while testing #3889. I have the full glog trace (heartbeat takes the task, backend processes zero keys, NACK goes back, master cleans the marker) if useful.

comments.author: feichai0017
comments.body:
Confirmed on upstream main **`b7595de3fab45a580e4ee8819c2a2940d43183cd`** in an independent Mooncake checkout, with production sources unchanged and no OrbitKV code. I also reproduced the stale-data **rescan path** mentioned in the report, with the scope described below.

### Reproduction results

The test-only patch below uses the existing `FileStorageTest` fixture with the production embedded Master, `Client`, `FileStorage`, and `BucketStorageBackend`. It performs actual puts/gets and disk I/O. Offload heartbeats, `OffloadObjects`, and recovery rescan are invoked synchronously to make the sequence deterministic; the FileStorage background scheduler is not started.

Environment: Debian 12 container, GCC 12.2, `USE_CUDA=OFF`, `USE_TENT=OFF`, classic TCP configured, bucket key limit 1, 4,109-byte values. This is a single-process **Store** reproducer, not a TENT or cross-host transport test.

| Case | Results over separate process runs | Observation after the second put |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Remove + re-put the same key with different bytes | 3/3 reproduce; exit 1 | New value reads correctly from memory; no LOCAL_DISK replica; backend still returns the complete old value |
| Same sequence, then call production `ReRegisterOffloadedObjects()` | 3/3 reproduce; exit 1 | LOCAL_DISK count changes from 0 to 1, while the backend still returns the complete old value |
| Fresh-key control for the second put | 3/3 pass; exit 0 | One LOCAL_DISK replica and the correct new disk bytes |
| Existing duplicate-only / mixed fresh-and-duplicate offload controls | Both pass; exit 0 | Existing skip/notification behavior remains intact |

Each round has a different deterministic byte pattern. The test compares all bytes, poisons the `Client::Get` destination, checks both boundary guards, and uses ordinary `Remove` only after the read lease expires. The first offload and disk-byte check pass in all runs. The next heartbeat after the second offload returns zero tasks.

Representative second-round observations:

```text
same_key=1 rescan=0 disk_replicas_before_rescan=0 disk_replicas_after_rescan=0 disk_matches_current=0 disk_matches_previous=1 next_heartbeat_tasks=0
same_key=1 rescan=1 disk_replicas_before_rescan=0 disk_replicas_after_rescan=1 disk_matches_current=0 disk_matches_previous=1 next_heartbeat_tasks=0
same_key=0 rescan=0 disk_replicas_before_rescan=1 disk_replicas_after_rescan=1 disk_matches_current=1 disk_matches_previous=0 next_heartbeat_tasks=0
```

The rescan result proves that the production rescan/registration path can attach a disk replica backed by old bytes to the new object. I have **not** tested an actual Master restart/HA transition, nor a subsequent user `Get` forced onto that disk replica. The new-value `Client::Get` check in this reproducer happens before rescan; the stale-byte observation is a direct backend `BatchLoad` afterward.

### Root cause and proposed fix

One refinement to the trace in the issue: in this sequential reproduction, the stale entry is filtered **before `BatchOffload`**, by the `IsExist(key)` check in [`GroupOffloadingKeysByBucket`](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/blob/b7595de3fab45a580e4ee8819c2a2940d43183cd/mooncake-store/src/storage_backend.cpp#L2356). [`OffloadObjects`](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/blob/b7595de3fab45a580e4ee8819c2a2940d43183cd/mooncake-store/src/file_storage.cpp#L545) NACKs keys skipped during grouping, and the Master clears the offload task. Fixing only the duplicate check inside `BatchOffload` would miss this path.

For rescan, `ReRegisterOffloadedObjects` reports persisted metadata through `NotifyOffloadSuccess`. With no pending offload task, the Master falls back to replica registration for the current key. `OffloadTaskItem` carries tenant/key/size, and `StorageObjectMetadata` carries location/size, but neither carries the object incarnation needed to distinguish the old and new values. Equal key and size are insufficient; both values in the reproducer deliberate
